From a mechanistic standpoint, evidence from preclinical models, particularly T-DXd-related studies, suggests that important events in ADC- ILD may involve target-independent processes, including Fcγ receptor-mediated sequestration of intact ADCs by alveolar macrophages, subsequent liberation of the payload into lysosomes, and bystander injury to alveolar epithelial cells; this cascade may trigger inflammatory amplification via the upregulation of secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) and contribute to fibrotic remodeling. This mechanistic paradigm supports a "safety-by-design" approach for the next-generation of ADC engineering, including Fc optimization, linker stabilization, payload permeability rationalization, and DAR optimization; this review establishes a conceptual basis for safer ADC development and better clinical risk stratification, framing ILD as a potentially predictable and structure-modulated toxicity, rather than an entirely idiosyncratic adverse event. It must be emphasized that the proposed FcγR-macrophage-SPP1 axis remains predominantly supported by murine and in vitro data, and its generalization across all ADC constructs and validation in human pulmonary tissue require further investigation.

articles.title: Liver-targeted drug delivery systems of traditional Chinese medicine: a novel strategy for the treatment of fatty liver disease.
articles.abstract: Fatty liver disease (FLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide, and its prevalence continues to rise steadily each year. FLD is not only a major predisposing factor for liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, but is also closely associated with various extrahepatic diseases such as cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, imposing a heavy burden on global healthcare systems. Currently, treatment options for FLD are limited. In contrast, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has a long history in treating FLD and has shown certain efficacy. However, most TCM compounds face limitations, including poor water solubility, low in vivo bioavailability, and insufficient liver-targeting ability, which hinder their effective accumulation at hepatic lesion sites. This article reviews the TCM monomer compounds used in the treatment of FLD, as well as the characteristics and recent advances in passive liver-targeting drug delivery systems, active liver-targeting systems, and smart drug-targeting systems. It also elucidates the challenges and development prospects of liver-targeting strategies in TCM therapeutic applications, aiming to promote the clinical translation and application of novel liver-targeted delivery drugs derived from TCM for the treatment of FLD.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese medicine interventions and mitochondrial communication in myocardial and cerebral ischemia: a critical review.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke share mitochondrial disturbances, but evidence that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) interventions regulate mitochondrial communication rather than general mitochondrial injury remains uncertain. This critical review evaluates that distinction. A structured search of PubMed, Lens Scholarly Search, and CNKI from inception to 28 August 2026 identified 1,663 records; 29 reports (24 preclinical/mechanistic and 5 clinical or systematic-review reports) informed the focused evidence map. We organized the evidence across four levels: intramitochondrial coordination, communication among mitochondria, contacts between mitochondria and other organelles, and intercellular mitochondrial signaling. Selected formulations, botanical drugs, and plant metabolites were associated most consistently with calcium-redox balance, bioenergetics, mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and immune-metabolic responses. However, most studies measured static proteins or downstream injury markers, used preventive dosing or poorly defined exposure, and did not test direct target engagement. Evidence for altered organelle contacts or transfer of intact mitochondria was sparse. Clinical studies of selected standardized commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations reported possible functional benefits, but product heterogeneity, trial limitations, and the absence of mitochondrial pharmacodynamic biomarkers preclude mechanistic attribution. We therefore distinguish communication-specific evidence from pathway association and appraise product identity, exposure plausibility, causal validation, methodological quality, and clinical relevance. Future studies should use taxonomically authenticated and chemically characterized preparations, clinically achievable dosing, dynamic communication-specific assays, causal perturbation, and prospectively defined mitochondrial biomarkers. Current evidence supports mitochondrial communication as a useful hypothesis-generating framework, but not yet as an established clinical mechanism of TCM in myocardial or cerebral ischemia.

articles.title: Beyond classical synthetic lethality: how PARP inhibitor pharmacology contributes to antitumor activity in HR-proficient cancers.
articles.abstract: PARP inhibitors were developed on the principle of synthetic lethality, which predicts enhanced sensitivity in tumors with homologous recombination deficiency (HRD). Clinical trials have demonstrated benefits beyond germline BRCA-mutated disease (NOVA and ARIEL3), including modest progression-free survival improvements in genomically HRD-negative subgroups (PRIMA). However, negative genomic HRD testing does not necessarily indicate functional HR proficiency, and these findings do not establish mechanisms independent of synthetic lethality. This Review examines the pharmacological mechanisms that may contribute to PARP inhibitor activity beyond established BRCA-associated HRD. The four agents have distinct pharmacological profiles-differences in PARP trapping potency, off-target activities against kinases (DYRK1A/1B, PIM3, CDK16) and the non-kinase PARP16, and immune-modulatory effects-that extend activity beyond HRD. Beyond canonical BRCA-associated HRD, these activities map onto distinct conditional dependencies in individual tumor contexts: lineage-dependent oncoprotein stability in small cell lung cancer, genotype-dependent immune vulnerability in SPOP-mutant prostate cancer, and pharmacologically induced HR impairment in hepatocellular carcinoma, where a direct c-Met-PARP1 mechanism remains to be verified. On-target mechanisms (PARP trapping and downstream DNA-damage effects) are directly demonstrated, whereas individual off-target contributions to clinical efficacy remain largely correlative and require prospective validation. By organizing these mechanisms into a unifying framework, this review aims to guide off-target-aware PARP inhibitor selection, rational combination design, and the development of next-generation compounds, providing a framework for investigating context-dependent PARP inhibitor strategies beyond established HRD-associated indications.

articles.title: Targeting the cGAS-STING axis in Alzheimer's disease: neuroinflammation-centric therapeutic strategies and perspectives.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder traditionally characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles. However, the limited clinical efficacy of Aβ/tau-targeted therapies has redefined neuroinflammation as an active driver of AD pathogenesis. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) axis acts as a central hub connecting aberrant cytosolic nucleic acid sensing particularly mitochondrial DNA leakage induced by Aβ and tau pathologies to chronic innate immune activation. This review comprehensively elucidates the pathogenic mechanisms of the cGAS-STING axis in AD, detailing its cell-type-specific activation in microglia, astrocytes, and neurons, and its downstream propagation via type I interferons, NF-κB, and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, which collectively drive synaptic damage and neuronal loss. We critically evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies, including covalent/non-covalent small-molecule inhibitors (e.g., RU.521, H-151, PF-06928215, SN-011), PROTAC degraders, RNA-based therapies, and immunomodulatory natural products/traditional Chinese medicines (e.g., icariin, tetrahydroxy stilbene glucoside, compound danshen dripping pills). Furthermore, we explore clinical translation prospects, emphasizing cerebrospinal fluid cGAMP and exosomal phosphorylated STING as minimally invasive biomarkers, while addressing key hurdles in blood-brain barrier penetration, and off-target risks. Finally, we highlight future directions involving organoid-microfluidic chip models and precision medicine frameworks to facilitate personalized cGAS-STING-targeted immunotherapy for AD.

articles.title: Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na+ and Ca2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. Beyond protons, endogenous ligands, toxins, and small molecules modulate ASIC gating through direct or synergistic mechanisms. ASICs have emerged as key players in pain and psychiatric disorders. Tissue acidosis drives hyperalgesia via sustained ASIC activation, synaptic plasticity disruption, and central sensitization, thereby promoting chronic pain. In limbic circuits, ASIC1a expression in the amygdala, periaqueductal gray, and dorsal raphe nucleus links these channels to anxiety and depression, with ASIC1a antagonists demonstrating robust efficacy in preclinical models. Selective ASIC modulators represent promising therapeutic candidates for pain-psychiatric comorbidities. This review integrates ASIC biophysical properties with their molecular and circuit-level mechanisms in disease, offering a framework to guide future translational efforts targeting ASIC-mediated pathologies.

articles.title: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles in musculoskeletal disorders: a narrative review of mechanisms, therapeutic efficacy, and translational prospects.
articles.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs), including sarcopenia, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, and rheumatoid arthritis, impose a growing global health burden, yet therapeutic options remain limited. Plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs), natural nanomedicines with multi-target potential, are emerging as promising candidates. This review examines preclinical evidence on PDEVs in MSDs, focusing on mechanisms, efficacy, and prospects. Preclinical studies indicate four interrelated mechanisms: gut microbiota remodeling, mitochondrial quality control, inflammation inhibition, and oxidative stress alleviation. PDEVs balance bone formation and resorption. In muscle, they preserve myofiber integrity via gut-muscle axis signaling, restore mitochondrial activity, and inhibit ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation. In bone and joint, they promote osteoblast differentiation and chondrogenesis, suppress osteoclastogenesis, mitigate chondrocyte senescence, and inhibit synovial fibroblast activation. However, efficacy evidence remains limited because plant sources, isolation/characterization methods, models, doses, administration routes, and outcome assessments vary. Reporting of randomization, allocation concealment, blinding, sample-size calculation, and replication is often inadequate. Consequently, conclusions regarding PDEVs in MSDs remain hypothetical. Clinical translation requires standardized production, pharmacokinetic data, and long-term safety evaluation, as well as causal cross-species validation, multi-omics-based source screening, tissue-specific engineering, and rigorous trial validation.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential of natural product polysaccharides in hepatocellular carcinoma: from microenvironment modulation to combination strategies.
articles.abstract: Natural-product polysaccharides are being investigated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as modulators of immune, inflammatory, metabolic and treatment-response pathways. Preclinical studies describe effects on tumor-associated macrophages, gut-liver signaling, hypoxia-associated angiogenesis and tumor-cell survival, including apoptosis, autophagy and ferroptosis. These findings motivate combination strategies with locoregional treatment, kinase inhibitors, chemotherapy and immune checkpoint blockade, but enhanced combination activity does not by itself demonstrate pharmacological synergy. This narrative review integrates material identity, mechanistic evidence and clinical outcomes, distinguishing purified polysaccharides, incompletely characterized preparations, composite extracts or granules, and formulation-enabled systems. Randomized evidence for fucoidan with transarterial chemoembolization and Huaier granule after resection provides product- and setting-specific signals; observational studies and immune-marker analyses offer less certain evidence of patient benefit. Clinical findings for composite products cannot establish the efficacy of isolated polysaccharides. Translation requires reproducible composition and dosing, exposure and interaction studies, safety assessment in impaired liver function, and controlled trials with clinically meaningful endpoints. Natural-product polysaccharides offer an experimental adjunctive framework, while definitive clinical utility for chemically defined products remains to be established.

articles.title: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation: molecular mechanisms and exploration of candidate therapeutic pathways.
articles.abstract: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM), formerly termed congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation, is a heterogeneous developmental lung disorder characterized by abnormal cystic or adenomatous structures. Its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood and may involve disturbed lung branching morphogenesis, altered epithelial differentiation, imbalanced cell proliferation and apoptosis, focal somatic mutations, and abnormal epithelial-mesenchymal interactions. This comprehensive narrative review discusses molecular findings relevant to CPAM, including Hoxb-5, SOX2, NKX2.1/TTF-1, FGF10, WNT/BMP, EGFR, RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, ACSL5/WNT2B, FABP7, and TGF-β signaling. We distinguish evidence obtained directly from human CPAM tissue-including expression studies and somatic mutation analyses-from findings extrapolated from normal lung development, animal models, and other pulmonary disorders. Recent morphological, immunohistochemical, molecular, and single-cell studies support substantial histological and molecular heterogeneity, while the relationship between specific histological subtypes and precise developmental windows remains provisional. Chromosomal microarray analysis and sequencing may help identify selected genomic abnormalities, but most candidate pathways have not yet been validated as causal or clinically actionable targets. We summarize key evidence gaps and outline priorities for tissue-resolved profiling, functional validation in organoid and developmental models, and cautious assessment of therapeutic feasibility and safety. This review aims to provide a critical framework for interpreting current CPAM molecular evidence and guiding future translational research.

articles.title: Inter-organ interaction axes in systemic inflammation: network pathological mechanisms, pharmacological targets, and precision treatment strategies.
articles.abstract: Systemic inflammation plays a central role in both acute and chronic pathological states. Acute inflammation is often triggered by infections or trauma, characterized by rapid immune activation low-grade inflammation is closely associated with aging-related diseases such as cardiovascular diseases and diabetes. During disease progression, inter-organ communication forms dynamic networks mediated by metabolites, immune factors, and neural signals, further amplifying the inflammatory response. This article focuses on three key inter-organ interaction axes: the gut-liver-brain axis, the adipose-muscle-bone axis, and the heart-kidney-lung axis. It discusses microbiota-driven metabolic neuroinflammation, immune-metabolic imbalance-induced tissue remodeling, and endothelial and microcirculatory damage in the context of multi-organ inflammation. Based on axis-specific molecular targets and spatiotemporal precision, pharmacological strategies are shifting from single-factor interventions to multitarget combination therapies. Meanwhile, innovative technologies such as single-cell multi-omics, spatial omics, artificial intelligence (AI), and organ-on-a-chip are expediting precision medicine approaches for the individualized treatment of systemic inflammation.

articles.title: Beyond class assumptions: a clinical decision framework for navigating drug-supplement interactions in oncology.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dietary supplement use is common among patients with cancer, with nearly half reporting concurrent use alongside conventional therapy. Despite widespread use, drug-supplement interactions in oncology are often difficult to interpret due to heterogeneous evidence, outdated case reports, reliance on in vitro and animal data, and a traditional focus on drug class effects rather than drug-specific vulnerability. Translation of preclinical findings is further complicated by host factors such as inflammation, pharmacogenomic variability, and the gut microbiome. The purpose of this review is to provide a mechanistic overview of drug-supplement interactions in oncology and characterize the existing literature to support clinical decision-making. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes current literature on pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions between dietary supplements and anticancer therapies, focusing on key mechanistic domains, including drug metabolism (CYP450 and UDP-glucuronosyltransferase enzymes), transporter systems, and immune modulation, and clinically relevant uncertainty. Interaction risk was evaluated across major anticancer drug classes, including tyrosine kinase inhibitors, hormonal therapies, oral chemotherapies, and immune checkpoint inhibitors. RESULTS: Interaction vulnerability varies substantially by drug class but is not uniform across individual agents. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors have substantial interaction potential due to CYP3A4 dependence, exposure-response relationships, and, for some agents, narrow therapeutic margins, with vulnerability varying by agent. Hormonal therapies present mechanism-specific risks, particularly CYP2D6-mediated activation of tamoxifen. Oral chemotherapies demonstrate variable interaction potential, with capecitabine associated with increased bleeding risk and cyclophosphamide dependent on CYP-mediated activation. Immune checkpoint inhibitors are less susceptible to metabolic interactions but present interpretation challenges related to immune modulation and emerging microbiome-related evidence, where theoretical risks often exceed clinical evidence. Across drug classes, many reported interactions remain theoretical, are derived from non-clinical data, or lack standardized product verification, limiting clinical interpretation. CONCLUSION: Drug-supplement interaction risk in oncology is best understood through a mechanism-based, drug-specific framework rather than isolated supplement-based or class-level approaches. A structured assessment incorporating drug metabolism, supplement activity, host factors, and clinical context may improve risk stratification and patient counseling, although management remains challenging in the absence of robust clinical data. Routine medication reconciliation and increased patient disclosure remain essential to minimizing avoidable harm and supporting safe, individualized cancer care.

articles.title: Nicotine dose effect function and actions of monoamine oxidase inhibiting drug on nicotine self-administration in female rats.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Rationale Tobacco is addictive and nicotine is the primary psychoactive chemical in tobacco. Nicotine is reliably self-administered in rat models, but, unlike stimulants and opiates, it is only weakly reinforcing. OBJECTIVES: Are there other tobacco chemicals that potentiate nicotine self-administration? METHODS: Adult female Sprague-Dawley rats were examined for impacts of monoamine oxidase inhibiting (MAOi) chemicals found in tobacco on nicotine self-administration (SA). In addition, a range of nicotine doses were investigated to determine potential impact of lowering nicotine levels modestly or substantially on its SA. The MAOi compounds, harmane, harmaline and 1-ethyl-β-carboline (EBC), were given to rats offered any of three different nicotine doses (3, 10 or 30 µg/kg/infusion). RESULTS: There was an inverted U-shaped dose-effect function of nicotine self-administration. Reduction of nicotine dose from the benchmark 30 to 10 µg/kg/infusion significantly increased self-administered infusions. A further lowering of nicotine from 10 to 3 µg/kg/infusion led to a significant decrease in SA. The three MAOi's given acutely over a range of relatively high doses had little or no effects on nicotine SA. Acute harmane caused a small, but significant, increase in nicotine SA, but only with the rats with lower than median nicotine self-administration. No impacts of acute doses of harmaline or EBC were seen. CONCLUSIONS: A non-monotonic dose-effect function of nicotine self-administration was found in female rats with higher than median baseline nicotine infusion rate, whereas rats with a lower than median rate had a monotonic function. Little or no interactive effects of MAOi's on nicotine self-administration were found.

articles.title: TIPE2/NF-κB signaling axis in osteosarcoma: mechanistic insights into its role in tumor progression.
articles.abstract: In this study, we examined the expression and cell-intrinsic function of TIPE2 in human osteosarcoma (OS). Notably, increased levels of TIPE2 expression have been observed in OS cell lines and tissues compared to normal cells and tissues, respectively. Furthermore, inhibition of TIPE2 expression through siRNA resulted in a marked reduction in the proliferative capacity, viability, and invasive characteristics of OS cells. This attenuation in OS cellular behavior was concomitant with observed alterations in autophagy-associated markers. In addition, the suppression of TIPE2 expression downregulated the expression of survivin, COX-2, cyclin A2, cyclin E, CDK-2, Runx2, MMP-9, N-cadherin, and Twist 1, while concurrently upregulated LC3B, E-cadherin, p62, p53, p21 and caspase-3. These alterations appear to be fundamentally associated with the NF-κB signaling cascade. Furthermore, our investigations revealed that the silencing of TIPE2 did not elicit significant changes in the expression levels of TNF-α, TNF-β, or TNFR1. However, it inhibited RANKL expression and NF-κB activation. Additionally, we demonstrated that silencing NF-κB does not influence TIPE2 expression, but the silencing of TNF-α and TNFR1 effectively inhibits TIPE2 expression. These observations suggest that TIPE2 operates downstream of TNF-α and TNFR1 but upstream of NF-κB. In summary, our findings identify TIPE2 as a candidate mediator of OS pathogenesis, and indicate that TIPE2 warrants further validation in vivo and in patient cohorts to establish it as a promising avenue for therapeutic intervention in OS.

articles.title: Targeting neuroinflammation in diabetic peripheral neuropathy: Mechanistic perspectives, phytochemical pharmacology, and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a debilitating neurodegenerative complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by the convergence of metabolic dysregulation, microvascular ischemia, and chronic low-grade neuroinflammation. While intensive glycemic control and cardiometabolic risk-factor modification slow neuropathy progression-most notably in type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM)-approved central analgesic pharmacotherapies primarily manage nociceptive symptoms without directly reversing established structural axonal loss. Preclinical studies indicate that endoneurial inflammation mediated via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB), and the nucleotide-binding domain, leucine-rich-containing family, pyrin domain-containing-3 (NLRP3) inflammasome contributes to microvascular dysfunction and Schwann cell dedifferentiation. Investigational phytochemicals, including curcumin, resveratrol, berberine, and quercetin, modulate these inflammatory and oxidative nodes in experimental rodent models. However, clinical translation remains constrained by poor aqueous solubility, extensive phase II enterocytic and hepatic conjugation, active efflux, and restricted transport across the diseased blood-nerve barrier (BNB). Using a structured narrative synthesis and a three-tier evidence hierarchy, this Brief Report distinguishes established human pathogenic and clinical trial evidence from preclinical mechanistic findings, critically evaluates clinical trial limitations (sample size, duration, and subjective endpoints), and defines rigorous pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic criteria required to validate nanocarrier-mediated endoneurial target engagement.

articles.title: Integrated population pharmacokinetic modeling of endogenous baseline and exogenous choline following oral choline alfoscerate administration.
articles.abstract: Choline alfoscerate is widely used to improve neurological function; however, choline is an endogenous compound that is constitutively present in the human body. Consequently, serum choline concentrations observed after drug administration represent the combined contribution of endogenous baseline levels and exogenous drug-derived choline, posing challenges for conventional pharmacokinetic (PK) interpretation. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a population pharmacokinetic (Pop-PK) model that integratively describes endogenous baseline choline and exogenous choline following single oral administration of choline alfoscerate. Pop-PK analysis was conducted using data from a bioequivalence study involving 36 healthy Korean male subjects. Model development followed a stepwise approach with systematic structural comparison and covariate screening. Endogenous baseline choline concentration was explicitly incorporated as an independent model component. A one-compartment model with an additive endogenous baseline component provided an empirical description of the observed serum choline concentration-time profiles, although the fitted exogenous kinetic parameters could not be independently identified as physiological processes. Inter-individual variability was identified for Ka and baseline endogenous choline concentration (BSL), and body mass index (BMI) was retained as a covariate on BSL in the final model. Internal goodness-of-fit, visual predictive check, and bootstrap diagnostics were examined; however, broad predictive intervals, temporal residual patterns, and uncertainty in selected random-effects parameters limited conclusions regarding predictive adequacy and parameter identifiability. These findings illustrate the potential utility and limitations of a constant-baseline population pharmacokinetic formulation for describing total serum choline concentrations, while further data and model evaluation are required before extrapolation to other dosing regimens or populations.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance of thromboembolic adverse events associated with osimertinib using the Japanese adverse drug event report database.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the disproportionality, times to onset, and outcomes of thromboembolic adverse events (AEs) associated with osimertinib using data from the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report database (JADER), with a specific focus on real-world evidence from Japan, an East Asian country with high EGFR mutation prevalence. We analyzed JADER data from April 2004 to December 2024. Disproportionality was assessed by calculating reporting odds ratios (RORs). Time-to-onset was evaluated, and Weibull distribution parameters were calculated for major AEs with detected signals, while rare AEs were summarized descriptively. Among 3,221,393 reports, 7134 AEs were associated with osimertinib, including 153 thromboembolic AEs. Significant disproportionality signals were detected for six thromboembolic AEs: deep vein thrombosis (ROR = 2.89), pulmonary embolism (ROR = 2.78), embolism venous (ROR = 6.64), peripheral vein thrombosis (ROR = 3.16), pulmonary artery thrombosis (ROR = 2.93), and thrombophlebitis migrans (ROR = 7.49). Median onset times ranged from 28 to 85 days after osimertinib initiation. Weibull analysis of major thromboembolic AEs suggested no clear time-dependent increase in reporting frequency over time (random failure type). Fatal outcomes were observed for several thromboembolic AEs, particularly pulmonary embolism and pulmonary artery thrombosis. Several thromboembolic AEs associated with osimertinib were identified, including potentially fatal events. These findings suggest that thromboembolic events may be reported relatively early after the initiation of osimertinib treatment and highlight the importance of clinical awareness and appropriate monitoring during treatment. However, these findings do not establish a causal relationship between osimertinib and thromboembolic events.

articles.title: Protective effects of intermittent fasting and vitamin E against hyperthyroidism-associated ocular complications in Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Our study endeavours to prevent hyperthyroidism-associated ocular complications through the synergy of intermittent fasting and vitamin E supplementation. Our aim was to reduce the incidence of hyperthyroidism-associated ocular complications by combining these two interventions, while carefully monitoring dietary intake and supplementing with vitamin E. In this experiment, animals were divided into normal, hyperthyroidism control, dual, vitamin E, and intermittent fasting groups. Hyperthyroidism was induced by administering thyroxine for 24 days. Animals in the treatment groups took vitamin E and practised intermittent fasting. Intraocular pressure was measured weekly during the protocol. After the protocol, antioxidant status, malondialdehyde and nitrite level, protein content, retinal pictures, histopathology of lens and thyroid profile were analysed. Rats with hyperthyroidism control exhibited elevated (p < 0.001) intraocular pressure, lipid peroxidation, total protein content, and thyroid hormone levels, while antioxidant and nitrite levels decreased (p < 0.001). However, our non-drug therapy significantly (p < 0.001) improved all of these parameters, bringing them to their optimum levels. Intermittent fasting prevented ocular disease caused by hyperthyroidism by reducing oxidative stress and fibro genic matter deposition, and modulating nitrite balance. It works best when combined with vitamin E for superior antioxidant benefits. Our proposed remedies not only improved ocular function but also provided physiological benefits, suggesting a link to metabolic, ophthalmic, and neurogenic diseases in future projections.

articles.title: Roxadustat for treatment of suspected erythropoietin(EPO)-induced pure red cell aplasia in a hemodialysis patient: a case report.
articles.abstract: Anemia is a prevalent complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly those undergoing dialysis. Recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) is widely administered to patients both on and off dialysis to manage this anemia. However, despite an initial favorable therapeutic response, a sudden and unexplained decline in hemoglobin (Hb) levels often prompts the need for further diagnostic evaluation. In this context, we report a clinical case involving a 48-year-old male patient who had been undergoing hemodialysis (HD) for two years. During the course of his rhEPO treatment regimen, he may have developed pure red cell aplasia (PRCA), a rare but serious adverse reaction. Upon recognition of this complication, the administration of rhEPO was promptly discontinued, and the patient was initiated on roxadustat therapy. Following nine months of continuous roxadustat treatment, the patient experienced a significant and sustained increase in his Hb levels. This clinical outcome underscores the importance of prompt diagnosis and intervention in cases of suspected erythropoietin (EPO)-induced PRCA. Furthermore, our findings suggest that roxadustat may serve as a viable and effective therapeutic option for patients with suspected EPO-induced PRCA, potentially obviating the need for immunosuppressive therapy and its associated risks.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of adjunctive use of rifaximin in preventing radiotherapy-induced diarrhea in cancer patients: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Radiation-induced diarrhea (RID) is a common, dose-limiting toxicity in patients with pelvic cancer undergoing radiotherapy. No pharmacological agent is currently approved for its prevention. Rifaximin, a non-absorbable antibiotic with anti-inflammatory and microbiota-modulating properties, may offer protective benefits. This prospective, parallel-group, open-label randomized controlled trial enrolled 80 adults with non-metastatic pelvic cancers receiving curative-intent radiotherapy, with or without chemotherapy. Participants were randomized in 1:1 ratio to receive standard care alone or standard care plus rifaximin 550 mg twice daily throughout radiotherapy. Primary outcome was the incidence of grade ≥ 2 diarrhea assessed by Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE v5.0). Secondary outcomes included time to diarrhea onset, stool consistency (Bristol scale), dehydration, quality of life assessed using European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30), and safety. Patients' follow-up lasted 3 months post-radiotherapy. Seventy-eight patients completed the study. Incidence of grade ≥ 2 diarrhea was comparable between groups (23.1% control vs. 17.9% rifaximin; risk difference [95% CI] - 5.1 [ - 23.0, 12.8]). Time to onset and rescue medication use did not differ significantly. Stool consistency and dehydration rates were comparable. Rifaximin significantly improved global health status at end of radiotherapy (mean difference between control and rifaximin groups [95% CI] - 10.5 [ - 18.5, - 2.4]) and at three months (- 7.0 [ - 13.1, - 1.0]), with lower fatigue (14.5 [4.2, 24.9]) and pain scores (12.8 [3.1, 22.5]). Adverse events were mild and comparable between groups. Adjunctive rifaximin did not reduce incidence or severity of RID but was associated with improved quality of life and symptom burden. Rifaximin was well tolerated. Larger, double-blind trials are warranted to confirm these findings and explore optimized dosing and timing of administration. Registration of the study: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06783153.

articles.title: Integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analysis identifies quercetin as a potential therapeutic candidate for osteoarthritis by targeting inflammation-related hub genes.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is closely associated with inflammatory activation, chondrocyte phenotypic alteration, and remodeling of the joint microenvironment. However, the key molecular network underlying these changes and its druggable targets remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify OA-related hub genes and explore the potential therapeutic relevance of quercetin through integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between OA and control samples were screened using the GSE55235 dataset. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify phenotype-related modules. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting DEGs, key module genes, and OA-associated genes from GeneCards. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed, followed by hub gene selection using multiple Cytoscape algorithms. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses, single-cell analysis based on GSE169454, drug prediction, and molecular docking were then performed. Finally, the effects of quercetin on hub gene expression were examined in LPS-stimulated immortalized chondrocytes. A total of 1022 DEGs were identified, and the turquoise module containing 597 genes was selected by WGCNA. Intersecting DEGs, module genes, and GeneCards-derived genes yielded 127 candidate genes. Five hub genes, namely, IL6, PTPRC, VEGFA, MYC, and NFKBIA, were further identified. Enrichment analyses linked these genes to inflammatory response, immune regulation, cell adhesion, NF-κB signaling, TNF signaling, and osteoclast differentiation. Single-cell analysis revealed heterogeneous expression of hub genes across chondrocyte subpopulations and microenvironment-related cells. Drug prediction and molecular docking suggested favorable binding between quercetin and the five hub proteins. In vitro experiments confirmed that quercetin reduced LPS-induced expression of VEGFA, PTPRC, NFKBIA, MYC, and IL-6. This study identifies five OA-related hub genes and suggests that quercetin may protect chondrocytes by modulating inflammatory and NF-κB-associated signaling.

articles.title: Brain disorders susceptibility induced by environmental pollutant lindane: possible phytotherapy amelioration by ferulic acid.
articles.abstract: Lindane (LIN) is an organochlorine pesticide with well-documented neurotoxic, genotoxic, and pro-oxidant properties. Owing to its environmental persistence and bioaccumulation, LIN can induce oxidative stress, DNA damage, apoptosis, and neuroinflammatory responses. This study aimed to investigate LIN-induced cellular toxicity and evaluate the potential protective effects of ferulic acid (FA) in C6, CTX TNA2, and RHiN neural cells. Oxidative stress parameters, including total antioxidant status (TAS), total oxidant status (TOS), and oxidative stress index (OSI), were evaluated. DNA damage was assessed using the comet assay, while apoptosis was determined using the TUNEL assay. Additionally, TLR1-10 gene and protein expression levels were analyzed to evaluate alterations in inflammatory signaling. LIN altered oxidative stress-related parameters, DNA damage, apoptotic cell death, and TLR expression across the three cell types. Notably, the oxidative stress response varied between cell lines, with OSI decreasing in LIN-treated CTX TNA2 cells. In contrast, FA treatment was associated with changes in antioxidant and oxidative stress-related parameters; however, potential interference of FA with the TAS assay should be considered when interpreting its apparent antioxidant effects. Comet and TUNEL assays further revealed treatment-related changes in DNA damage and apoptosis, while TLR expression changes varied according to cell type and treatment. LIN-induced cellular responses differed among the neural cell models examined. FA may modulate some of the effects associated with LIN exposure; however, the interpretation of TAS findings requires caution because of potential assay interference. These findings highlight the importance of considering cell-specific responses and assay-related limitations when evaluating the potential protective effects of FA against LIN-induced neural damage.

articles.title: Development of a Clinical Decision Support Tool for Drug Dose Adjustment Based on Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate.
Strengthening medicine availability through enhanced international collaboration: Outcomes from a pilot on global regulatory assessment of manufacturing changes.
articles.abstract: Medicine shortages continue to represent a critical global health challenge. While causes are multifactorial, issues can be mitigated by measures that increase manufacturing capacity. However, these require regulatory approval, often across multiple jurisdictions, and between-regulator differences in regulatory systems, data requirements and approval timelines can make global approval complex and time consuming. To address this challenge, the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) launched a pilot programme in which five submissions went through collaborative review of the same chemistry, manufacturing and control (CMC) data by up to eight global regulatory authorities, aiming to deliver harmonized outcomes using science and risk-based assessment principles. A standardized 120-day review process was established, enabling near-simultaneous approvals across participating regions. Most (88%) assessment questions were harmonized; alignment reduced the number of questions by 25% compared with independent reviews. These results demonstrate that global regulatory collaboration can significantly accelerate implementation of manufacturing changes, strengthen supply chains and help to mitigate medicine shortages. Efforts are underway to develop this into a sustainable global regulatory approach.

articles.title: Association Between Urinary pH and Vancomycin-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vancomycin (VCM) is an antibiotic widely used to treat Gram-positive bacterial infections but commonly causes severe acute kidney injury (AKI). Because VCM contains an amino group with a pKa of 7.2 and has an isoelectric point of 7.2, its ionization state may depend on urinary pH, potentially influencing susceptibility to VCM-associated AKI (VCM-AKI). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to clarify the relationship between urinary pH and VCM-AKI. METHODS: This study analysed patients whose urinary pH was measured during intravenous VCM treatment at Chiba University Hospital between April 2013 and December 2024. The onset of VCM-AKI was determined using a modified KDIGO 2012 criteria. A multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with VCM-AKI. RESULTS: The number of analysed patients without and with AKI were 437 and 50, respectively. The multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that intensive care unit admission, loop diuretics use, serum VCM trough concentration and urinary pH (odds ratio, 0.69; 95% confidence interval, 0.48-0.98; p = 0.04) were significantly associated with VCM-AKI. CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this retrospective study suggest that urinary pH is significantly associated with VCM-AKI in hospitalized patients. Further prospective studies are needed to validate this association.

articles.title: Spotlight Commentary: Drug-induced liver injury-Novel biomarkers and epigenetic insights.
Higher daily dietary quercetin intake attenuated the association between blood cadmium and depressive symptom risk: a NHANES-based cross-sectional study and animal experimental validation.
articles.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a highly toxic heavy metal that can accumulate in brain tissue, inducing oxidative stress and inflammation, thereby contributing to the pathogenesis of depression. Quercetin, a natural flavonoid with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, shows potential against exogenous toxicity and neurological diseases. However, epidemiological evidence on whether quercetin modifies the association between Cd exposure and depression risk is limited, and the underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. First, a cross-sectional analysis was conducted using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) database to investigate the modifying effect of dietary quercetin intake on the association between blood Cd levels and depressive symptoms. Subsequently, in vivo animal experiments were performed to evaluate whether quercetin ameliorates Cd-induced depressive-like behaviors and to explore the potential mechanisms via metallomic profiling. The population-based observational analysis revealed that higher blood Cd burden was significantly positively associated with an increased risk of depressive symptoms, whereas higher daily dietary quercetin intake was associated with a reduced risk of Cd-related depressive symptoms. In the animal experiments, quercetin (50 mg/kg·bw) attenuated anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors and spatial memory deficits induced by subchronic CdCl2 exposure in rats. Mechanistically, metallomic and biochemical analyses suggested that quercetin may modulate NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling in the prefrontal cortex by exerting antioxidant effects and restoring elemental homeostasis, thereby alleviating Cd-induced neurobehavioral alterations. Collectively, this study provides observational evidence linking dietary quercetin to a reduced risk of Cd-related depressive symptoms, and in animal experiments found that quercetin can alleviate Cd-induced depressive-like and anxiety-like behaviors in rats. These findings suggest that quercetin could serve as a potential dietary supplement against Cd-induced neurotoxicity.

articles.title: Selenium deficiency aggravates cadmium-induced liver fibrosis through oxidative stress/HIF-1α/ENO1 pathway-mediated H3K18 lactylation modification.
articles.abstract: Heavy metal cadmium (Cd) exposure is a widespread global environmental risk factor that can induce liver injury. Selenium (Se) is an essential nutritional trace element, and its deficiency is an important pathological marker of the liver. However, the role of Se deficiency in Cd-induced liver injury and its underlying mechanisms are still unclear. In this study, by using a porcine model and hepatic parenchymal cell lines, we found that Se deficiency significantly aggravated Cd-induced liver fibrosis and evaluated the expression levels of proinflammatory factors and fibrotic marker genes. Mechanistically, Se deficiency and Cd exposure synergistically induced excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and activated hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α)-mediated transcription expression of the key glycolytic enzyme α-enolase (ENO1), thereby leading to glycolysis-related metabolic alterations, including increased lactate and decreased ATP. Further studies showed that lactate acted as an epigenetic signal, significantly enhancing lactylation at the histone-H3-lysine-18 site (H3K18la). Notably, pharmacological inhibition of ENO1 with AP-III-a4 reduces lactate production, H3K18la levels, and fibrosis-related gene expression, which could be reversed by exogenous lactate supplementation. In summary, our findings demonstrate that Se deficiency drives H3K18 lactylation via the oxidative stress/HIF-1α/ENO1 axis to exacerbate Cd exposure-induced liver fibrosis, offering a redox-centric perspective on their synergistic pathogenic mechanism.

articles.title: Bergenin attenuates osteoclast-mediated bone loss by modulating the SIRT1/NF-κB p65 signalling axis.
articles.abstract: Current pharmacological treatments for osteoporosis are often accompanied by clinically significant adverse effects, highlighting the need for safer therapeutic strategies. Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) suppresses inflammatory responses and osteoclast differentiation, suggesting its therapeutic potential. Bergenin is known to activate SIRT1, although its effects on osteoporosis and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. Hence, we aimed to identify a mechanistic rationale for the therapeutic application of bergenin in the treatment of osteoporosis. We first examined SIRT1 expression in femoral tissue from patients with osteopenia and osteoporosis. The role of SIRT1 and efficacy of bergenin were then investigated using myeloid cell-specific SIRT1 knockout (SIRT1fl/fl-LysMCre) mice, ovariectomised models, and osteoclastogenesis in bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) following RANKL stimulation. SIRT1 expression was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissue, while myeloid cell-specific SIRT1 deficiency aggravated ovariectomy (OVX)-induced bone loss. Bergenin preserved bone microarchitecture and inhibited osteoclast differentiation in OVX mice; these effects were weakened by the SIRT1 inhibitor, EX527. Mechanistically, bergenin activated SIRT1, diminished both the phosphorylation and acetylation of NF-κB p65, prevented NF-κB pathway activation, and suppressed osteoclast differentiation. To our knowledge, this study provides the first clinical evidence linking SIRT1 to osteoporosis in human bone specimens. These findings suggest that bergenin acts through the SIRT1/NF-κB p65 pathway and provide a rationale for developing bergenin as a naturally derived therapy for osteoporosis and related osteoclast-driven skeletal disorders.

articles.title: Aerobic exercise attenuates hippocampal mitochondrial fragmentation and preserves synaptic integrity in an AD-like rat model: Associations with FNDC5/Irisin and Drp1-related mitochondrial fission.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a major neurodegenerative disorder without an effective cure. This study explores the effect of aerobic exercise (AE) on hippocampal mitochondrial fission and synaptic integrity in an AD-like rat model. METHODS: The AD-like rat model was induced by D-galactose and sodium nitrite, with AE administered concurrently. An Aβ25-35-induced PC12 cell model was used to examine the effects of exogenous Irisin. KEY FINDING: AE ameliorated cognitive deficits and reduced hippocampal Aβ42 levels, while increasing synaptic density and PSD95 and SYP expression during the formation process of AD. The AD-like model exhibited mitochondrial fragmentation and increased p-Drp1/Drp1, accompanied by reduced FNDC5/Irisin levels in skeletal muscle, plasma, and hippocampus. AE intervention attenuated these alterations. Exercise-associated hippocampal Irisin changes may involve peripheral skeletal muscle-derived Irisin, although its precise tissue origin remains unclear. In PC12 cells, Irisin supplementation effectively mitigated mitochondrial fragmentation and the increase in p-Drp1/Drp1, suggesting a potential association between Irisin and Drp1-related mitochondrial fission. SIGNIFICANCE: Thus, AE may attenuate cognitive impairment and hippocampal mitochondrial fission while preserving synaptic integrity, with potential involvement of FNDC5/Irisin signaling and Drp1-associated mitochondrial fission.

articles.title: Xihuang pill-induced reprogramming of tumor-associated macrophages to suppress glioblastoma progression is associated with the mTOR/autophagy-DAMP axis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Xihuang pill has shown antitumor activity in various cancers; however, its immunomodulatory mechanisms in glioblastoma remain incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate whether Xihuang pill regulates tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) polarization and functional status in glioblastoma microenvironment, and to elucidate the involvement of the mTOR/autophagy pathway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used peripheral blood from Xihuang pill-treated glioblastoma patients, along with glioblastoma cell lines and macrophage models in both co-culture systems and intracranial xenograft mouse models. Macrophage polarization, migration, invasion, and phagocytosis were assessed by flow cytometry, transwell assays, confocal microscopy, and phagocytosis assays. Protein expression was examined by western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Autophagy markers and DAMPs release were evaluated, and transcriptome sequencing was performed to profile cytokine alterations. RESULTS: Xihuang pill promoted M1 polarization in patient blood and experimental models, with increased CD68+CD86+ populations and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IFN-γ, iNOS), alongside reduced M2 markers (IL-4, IL-10, IL-13, Arg-1). Mechanistically, it inactivated mTOR and activated autophagy in glioblastoma cells, as indicated by increased Beclin-1 expression, elevated LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, and decreased p62 levels. This autophagic activation triggered DAMPs including calreticulin, ATP, and HMGB1, which reprogrammed macrophages toward M1. Xihuang pill attenuated macrophage infiltration and migration, restored phagocytic function, and suppressed tumor cell proliferation. Rapamycin partially mimicked these effects, whereas autophagy inhibitors exerted opposite regulatory actions. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal a novel mechanism by which Xihuang pill reprograms tumor-associated macrophages to shift the immunosuppressive glioblastoma microenvironment toward an immunoactivated phenotype, an effect associated with the mTOR/autophagy-DAMP axis. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2300071982.

articles.title: Biochemical and biophysical evaluation of the effects of phytochemicals isolated from Ziziphus mucronata on Plasmodium falciparum heat shock protein 70-1 (PfHsp70-1).
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ongoing Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) resistance to first-line treatment threatens the livelihoods of people in Sub-Saharan African tropical regions, necessitating the development of new antimalarials. Ziziphus mucronata (Z. mucronata) is a native South African medicinal plant, used in Traditional Southern African Medicine to treat malaria. Its antimalarial properties have been validated, but its phytochemistry remains largely unexplored. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to isolate bioactive compounds from the dichloromethane bark extract of Z. mucronata and evaluate their inhibitory potential against Plasmodium falciparum Heat shock protein 70-1 (PfHsp70-1), a molecular chaperone whose inhibition has been linked to parasite death. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Isolation of compounds was done using bioassay-guided isolation, followed by structural elucidation and characterisation using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and distortionless enhancement by polarization transfer (DEPT-135). The antiplasmodial activity of the bioactive compounds was determined against the chloroquine-sensitive P. falciparum (NF54) strain to establish baseline efficacy, and the haemolytic activity was tested on non-parasitised human red blood cells. The binding potential of the compounds to PfHsp70-1's ATP-binding pocket was explored computationally using molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Their effects on the molecular chaperone's structure and function were assessed experimentally using far-ultraviolet (UV) circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy and a lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) aggregation assay. RESULTS: Two primary active compounds, oleanolic acid (OA) and betulinic acid (BA), were successfully isolated. OA exhibited potent antimalarial activity (IC50 at 1.71 ± 0.19 μM) and low haemolysis (2.24 ± 1.05%) at 10 μM, whereas BA showed moderate activity (IC50 = 10.39 ± 4.10 μM) and negligible haemolysis (0.11 ± 0.12%) at 10 μM. OA (- 6. 346 kcal/mol) showed a high binding affinity for PfHsp70-1 compared to BA (- 5.720 kcal/mol). MD simulations revealed that both compounds form stable interactions with PfHsp70-1, although OA interacts with more residues compared to BA. Far-UV CD spectroscopy showed that protein unfolding at high concentrations (500 - 1000 μM) was induced by BA, whereas OA elicited a stable conformational change at a lower concentration (250 μM). CONCLUSION: This study isolated OA for the first time in Z. mucronata and demonstrates its potential as an inhibitor of PfHsp70-1.

articles.title: Structural characterization, functional assessment, and process origin analysis of glucuronidation in a therapeutic monoclonal antibody.
articles.abstract: Glucuronidation is a previously reported (though typically at low levels) acidic post-translational modification (PTM) of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies, arising from the proposed non-enzymatic covalent conjugation of glucuronic acid to both N-terminal and surface lysine residues, resulting in a molecular mass increase of approximately 176 Da per modification. Despite its prevalence, glucuronidation remains poorly characterized, with limited information on structural features, functional impact, and process origin. In this study, we used a therapeutic IgG4 monoclonal antibody (mAb1) as a model to systematically investigate these aspects. Using two-dimensional liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (2D-LC/MS), ion exchange chromatography (IEX) -enriched fraction, and peptide mapping, nine glucuronidation sites were identified across both light and heavy chains, and the glucuronidated species were found to be one of the contributors to the acidic charge variant profile, markedly enriched in the acidic region. Stressed glucuronidation samples at modification levels exceeding the normal process range showed no consistent decrease in antigen binding or bioactivity (evaluated up to 79.53% glucuronidation); FcRn binding affinity and non-specific binding were similar to the control in the tested mixtures (evaluated at approximately 19% glucuronidation). Quantification of free glucuronic acid across culture media and process intermediates revealed glucuronidation is generated or released during CHO cell culture, with its occurrence associated with the presence of free glucuronic acid in the culture environment. Glucuronidation was observed in the two IgG4 antibodies but in neither of the two IgG1 antibodies examined, a preliminary observation suggesting potential IgG subclass-related structural susceptibility, which requires validation with a larger sample set. These findings inform the molecule-specific assessment of glucuronidation and offer a generalizable framework for the risk assessment and control strategy development of other reported PTMs in similar molecules from a CMC control perspective. The functional conclusions are restricted to the in vitro attributes evaluated in this study.

articles.title: Stirring the Pot: Surprising Observation of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)-Containing Particles When Stir-stressing Biologic Formulations with PTFE-coated Stir Bars.
articles.abstract: Stirring of solutions is a common procedure in pharmaceutical processes, including homogenization of bench-scale solutions and large-scale manufacturing reactors, and providing mechanical shear in accelerated stress studies. One of the common mechanisms for stirring is to use a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE, Teflon™) stir bar in contact with a container interior surface. The stirring process has been assumed to produce protein particles through shearing of adsorbed protein film from the surface of the stir bar and that the components, typically glass and PTFE, did not contribute to the particle population. In this Lessons Learned Communication, the observation of PTFE particles liberated from the stir bar during stir stress of a surfactant-free formulation using infrared (IR) microspectroscopy is reported on. These PTFE particles are seen to be elongated in morphology and are also found to be coated with protein. This observation has practical implications owing to the prevalence of stir-stressing in biologics development and warrants rapid dissemination into the community.

articles.title: Interlaboratory Evaluation of the Multi‑attribute Method Across Japanese Pharmaceutical Companies: Variability of Post-Translational Modification and Recommendations for Standardization.
articles.abstract: The multi‑attribute method (MAM) is a promising LC/MS‑based approach for the simultaneous qualitative and quantitative assessment of critical quality attributes in therapeutic antibodies. However, its application to quality control is hindered by interlaboratory variability. To elucidate sources of such variability, a systematic interlaboratory comparison was conducted among six Japanese pharmaceutical companies using digested NIST monoclonal antibody reference materials. Each laboratory generated peptide‑mapping data under routine analytical conditions, enabling cross‑site evaluation of post‑translational modification (PTM) detection, annotation, and quantification. Substantial discrepancies were observed in the detection frequency and reported abundance of many PTMs, whereas a limited set of dominant attributes, including major glycans and N‑terminal modifications, showed high interlaboratory concordance. Detailed analyses identified multiple contributors to disagreement, such as differences in peptide identification criteria (MS1‑based versus MS/MS‑confirmed); inconsistent PTM reporting policies; variability in sample preparation and LC/MS parameters; charge‑state selection for quantification, particularly affecting C‑terminal lysine variants; and artifactual in‑line oxidation during analysis. Practical mitigation strategies were shown to reduce specific sources of variability, including methionine supplementation and chromatographic standardization. Overall, the study highlights the necessity of harmonizing identification, reporting, and data‑processing practices to enhance the robustness and reproducibility of MAM for routine antibody quality control.

articles.title: Inhibition of p38 MAPK signaling Alleviates Synovitis and Protects Joint Integrity in Hemophilic Arthropathy.
articles.abstract: Hemophilic arthropathy (HA) is a debilitating joint disorder triggered by recurrent hemarthrosis. Despite effective hematological prophylaxis, persistent synovial inflammation often leads to irreversible joint destruction. The precise mechanisms by which erythrocyte breakdown products sustain this inflammatory microenvironment remain elusive. To explore the underlying mechanisms, we developed an in vitro intra-articular hemolysis model through stimulating fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) with hemin. We examined FLS proliferation, migration, and invasion, and analyzed the expression of inflammatory cytokines. By using FLS conditioned medium, we assessed downstream chondrocyte oxidative stress and matrix degradation. Additionally, an HA rat model was utilized to assess joint pathology following p38 inhibition (SB203580). In vitro experiments demonstrated that hemin robustly activated p38 phosphorylation and upregulated pro-inflammatory mediators (IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), alongside promoting FLS proliferation, migration, and invasion. Mechanistically, pharmacological inhibition of p38 with SB203580 significantly suppressed these pathogenic phenotypes and indirectly protected chondrocytes against ROS accumulation and a catabolic shift (MMP3 upregulation and Collagen II degradation). The in vivo studies further revealed that the SB203580 administration effectively alleviated synovial hyperplasia, angiogenesis, hemosiderin deposition, and cartilage damage in HA. In conclusion, the inhibition of p38 MAPK signaling mitigated HA progression by suppressing synovitis and restoring chondrocyte matrix homeostasis, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic strategy for HA joint protection.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of azole antifungals identifies a shared side-chain structure associated with Th1-like response suppression.
articles.abstract: Azole antifungals are widely used in clinical practice and have been reported to modulate mammalian immune responses, independent of their antifungal activity. However, whether these effects are shared among azole antifungals and the structural features underlying these effects remain unclear. We assessed the effects of five azole antifungals using an allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) mouse model and splenic immune cell culture system under T helper 1 (Th1)-like conditions. Ear swelling and Th1-associated gene expression were assessed in a 2,4-dinitrofluorobenzene-induced ACD model and stimulated mouse splenocytes, respectively. Itraconazole and posaconazole significantly suppressed ear swelling and downregulated the mRNA expression of interferon-gamma (Ifng) and T-box transcription factor 21. Ketoconazole reduced Ifng mRNA expression at 10 μM but did not significantly reduce ear swelling, whereas fluconazole and voriconazole showed no significant effects in either assessment. We further assessed a triazolone derivative containing a side-chain region shared by itraconazole and posaconazole. The derivative significantly reduced ear swelling in the ACD model and suppressed Ifng mRNA expression in a concentration-dependent manner ex vivo. Our findings suggest that the shared partial side-chain structure may contribute to the immunomodulatory effects of specific azole antifungals.

articles.title: Geranylgeranylacetone Attenuates Atherosclerosis via the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 Signaling Axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading global health threat, driven by macrophage foam cell formation and chronic inflammation. Geranylgeranylacetone (GGA), an anti-ulcer drug known to induce heat shock proteins, may confer cardiovascular benefits, yet its direct anti-atherosclerotic mechanisms are not fully understood. METHODS: ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet received GGA (400 mg/kg/d) for 12 weeks. Atherosclerotic lesions, plaque composition (necrotic core, collagen, macrophage infiltration), plasma lipids, and cytokine levels were evaluated. In vitro, THP-1-derived foam cells were treated with Ox-LDL and GGA (0.1-100 μmol/L). Cholesterol efflux, lipid accumulation, and the expression of Matcap2, Apelin, ABCA1/ABCG1, apolipoproteins, and inflammatory factors were measured. siRNA silencing was used to validate the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 axis. RESULTS: GGA significantly reduced aortic plaque burden, increased collagen content, decreased macrophage infiltration, lowered total cholesterol, triglycerides, and LDL-C, raised HDL-C, and improved inflammatory cytokine profiles (decreased IL-6 and TNF-α; increased IL-10) in ApoE-/- mice. In foam cells, GGA enhanced cholesterol efflux, reduced cholesteryl ester content and lipid droplets, and upregulated Matcap2, Apelin, ABCA1/ABCG1, and ApoA1/A2/A4, while downregulating ApoB, IL-6, and TNF-α. Silencing either Matcap2 or Apelin abrogated GGA-induced upregulation of ABCA1/ABCG1, cholesterol efflux, and the protective apolipoprotein and anti-inflammatory phenotypes. CONCLUSION: GGA attenuates atherosclerosis by activating the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 signaling axis, thereby promoting reverse cholesterol transport and resolving inflammation. These findings support GGA as a promising repurposed drug with both cardioprotective and gastroprotective benefits.

articles.title: Targeting SHMT2 genetically and pharmacologically inhibits nasopharyngeal carcinoma progression via disruption of the SHMT2-SAM-m6A regulatory circuit and TNF/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: SHMT2, a key enzyme in one-carbon metabolism, provides biosynthetic intermediates and methyl donors required for tumor growth. Its biological and pharmacological relevance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) remains incompletely understood. Here, we showed that SHMT2 was markedly upregulated in NPC and associated with poorer prognosis. SHMT2 depletion and glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) treatment suppressed NPC cell proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth. GA treatment reduced intracellular S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), m6A enrichment on SHMT2 transcripts, IGF2BP3 association, and SHMT2 mRNA stability. METTL16- and IGF2BP3-depletion experiments implicated these regulators in SHMT2 transcript stabilization. Wild-type SHMT2 restored transcript-associated m6A enrichment more effectively than the K280A mutant, consistent with a contribution from SHMT2 catalytic activity. SAM supplementation counteracted GA-induced changes in SHMT2 expression, transcript-associated m6A enrichment, mRNA stability, and malignant phenotypes. In parallel, transcriptomic analysis implicated TNF signaling, and SHMT2 depletion reduced p65 phosphorylation, nuclear localization, NF-κB reporter activity, and TNF-responsive gene expression. TNF-α partially rescued the effects of SHMT2 depletion or GA treatment. These findings support a SAM-dependent contribution to SHMT2 transcript regulation and the functional involvement of TNF/NF-κB signaling in SHMT2-associated NPC phenotypes. The molecular connection between these regulatory processes remains unresolved, and the effects of GA cannot be attributed exclusively to SHMT2 inhibition.

articles.title: Targeting oxidative stress with resveratrol mitigates structural degeneration and sensory hyperexcitability in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a dose-limiting adverse effect of antineoplastic treatments, characterized by persistent sensory dysfunction and chronic pain. With no disease-modifying therapies available, targeting its underlying oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and structural nerve damage is critical. Resveratrol, a polyphenolic compound with robust redox-regulatory properties, represents a compelling candidate to intercept these neurodegenerative processes. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic effects and neuroprotective mechanisms of resveratrol in a mouse model of paclitaxel-induced CIPN. Following paclitaxel administration, resveratrol was administered daily from post-injection day (PID) 7 to 13. Our multidisciplinary approach integrated behavioral assessment of hypersensitivity, redox analyses, molecular and electrophysiological evaluations in dorsal root ganglia (DRG), ultrastructural examination of sural nerves, and intraepidermal nerve fiber (IENF) quantification in plantar skin. Resveratrol significantly attenuated mechanical hypersensitivity. In the DRG, resveratrol reduced oxidative stress-associated DHE fluorescence, accompanied by restoration of AMPK-PGC-1α signaling and SOD2 expression. Resveratrol also exerted structural protective effects, as evidenced by the recovery of myelin protein levels, improved sural nerve ultrastructure, and attenuation of IENF degeneration. Furthermore, voltage-sensitive dye imaging (VSDI) demonstrated that resveratrol attenuated aberrant stimulus-evoked neuronal hyperexcitability in the DRG. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that resveratrol alleviates paclitaxel-induced CIPN by reducing oxidative stress, preserving peripheral nerve integrity, and attenuating aberrant sensory neuronal activities. By targeting multiple pathological features of CIPN, resveratrol may represent a promising therapeutic approach for alleviating established effects.

articles.title: Luteolin, a component of Salvia miltiorrhiza, attenuates renal interstitial fibrosis progression by targeting the PTGS2-mediated inflammatory axis.
articles.abstract: The progressive decline of renal function in chronic kidney disease (CKD) inevitably culminates in renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF), yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking. While Salvia miltiorrhiza (SM) constitutes a rich reservoir of nephroprotective natural products, the precise chemical-protein interactions underlying its anti-fibrotic efficacy remain largely elusive. In the present study, a target-driven in silico screening was employed to identify the principal active component of SM and characterize its direct biophysical target. Computational analysis identified luteolin as the constituent exhibiting the highest binding affinity toward prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2/COX2). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed a highly stable luteolin-PTGS2 complex, which was experimentally authenticated by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), demonstrating a direct and strong biophysical interaction (KD = 2.73 μM). In vivo validation showed that luteolin administration significantly ameliorated renal dysfunction and attenuated extracellular matrix deposition in a folic acid-induced RIF mouse model. This protective phenotype was mechanistically linked to the suppression of PTGS2 and its downstream pro-inflammatory mediators (EP2, EP4, MCP-1, IL-1 β, and TNF-α). Cell experiments demonstrated that, consistently with the effects of the PTGS2 inhibitor meloxicam, luteolin reduced the expression of both the PTGS2 axis and pro-fibrotic proteins in RIF cell model. Furthermore, clinical data demonstrated that PTGS2 is significantly upregulated in human fibrotic kidneys and correlates inversely with renal function. In conclusion, as a component of SM, luteolin directly binds to and inhibits PTGS2, thereby blocking the downstream pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic cascades.

articles.title: Tenoxicam-loaded novasomal thermosensitive in situ gel for the alleviation of carrageenan-induced conjunctivitis: formulation, in vitro and in vivo studies.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop tenoxicam (TNX) -loaded novasomes (NOV) to enhance the drug ocular bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy for the alleviation of conjunctivitis. The formulations were prepared adopting thin-film hydration technique employing cholesterol, oleic acid and the non-ionic surfactant. Entrapment efficiency (EE %), vesicle size and zeta potential (ZP) were determined. Tenoxicam-loaded formulation prepared using Brij S20: oleic acid ratio of 2:1 (TNX-NOV4) was selected and incorporated into thermosensitive in situ gel. In vitro release experiment was conducted to investigate tenoxicam release behavior from the optimum formulation. In vivo experiments were performed on carrageenan-induced conjunctivitis rat model. Tenoxicam-loaded novasomes exhibited high EE% ranging from 93.32 ± 2.2 to 96.77 ± 0.69% and nanosize ranging between 174 ± 15.9 to 581 ± 18.6 nm. Vesicles had relatively high negative ZP values indicating good stability. Release of TNX from TNX-NOV4 (suspension and in situ gel) was biphasic. In vivo studies revealed that TNX-NOV4 in situ gel was superior in the alleviation of conjunctivitis in comparison with free-TNX in situ gel and a marketed eye drop. The inflammation score for TNX-NOV4 in situ gel demonstrated faster recovery. Biochemical investigations have established that treatment with TNX-NOV4 in situ gel suppressed the expression of interleukin 6 (IL-6), inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) , reduced nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) and elevated nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NrF2) eye tissues contents. The outcomes were confirmed by further histopathological investigations. Conclusively, novasomes could be considered as a novel distinguished nanoplatform to enhance ocular delivery of tenoxicam.

articles.title: Exploring the aryl hydrocarbon receptor/aldehyde oxidase relationship.
α-synuclein regulation of monoamine transporters: Implications for psychostimulant pharmacology and Parkinson disease.
Post-marketing safety signals of rabbit antithymocyte globulin in FAERS and JADER, 2004-2024.
articles.abstract: Rabbit antithymocyte globulin (rATG) is used in transplant immunosuppression, but spontaneous reports may reveal safety signals not apparent in clinical studies. We analyzed rATG-indexed reports in FAERS and JADER from 2004 through 2024 using four disproportionality methods. We also explored reported-sex and age subgroups, time to onset, and alternative drug-role inclusion criteria. At the preferred-term level, 357 signals met the prespecified criteria in FAERS and 108 in. JADER, with 87 overlapping signals. Thrombotic microangiopathy and hemorrhagic cystitis were potential signals not identified in the labeling comparison. Vomiting and enterococcal sepsis showed different subgroup-specific reporting patterns by sex, and infection-related signals appeared among reports for patients aged ≥65 years. Overall median time to onset was 10 days in FAERS (1622 reports) and 25 days in JADER (1292 reports). The corresponding medians for infections and infestations were 11 and 30 days. These case-only analyses describe reporting associations and recorded onset intervals, not incidence, comparative clinical risk, or causality. The findings warrant confirmation in studies with control with confounding. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This analysis compares rATG reporting patterns in two spontaneous-reporting databases and identifies potential signals, including Thrombotic microangiopathy and hemorrhagic cystitis, that warrant further evaluation. The databases do not provide exposed-population denominators or complete follow-up. Accordingly, disproportionality and TTO findings are hypothesis-generating and do not quantify clinical incidence or establish causality.

articles.title: Survexins and SurvexANs - novel nano-encapsulated inhibitors of Crm1-dependent nuclear export of Survivin.
articles.abstract: The inhibitor of apoptosis protein Survivin is frequently overexpressed in many cancers. Its nuclear export signal (NES) facilitates active transport into the cytoplasm, where Survivin interferes with apoptosis and thereby promotes cancer cell survival. Thus, blocking Survivin nuclear export via the nuclear export receptor Crm1/XPO1 represents a promising anticancer strategy. We identified two novel compounds, termed "Survexins," that inhibit Crm1-mediated nuclear export exhibiting distinct inhibition kinetics and reversibility. Both compounds inhibited NES-dependent nuclear export of our model biosensors including Survivin-NES biosensor and full-length Survivin in a dose-dependent manner and induced apoptosis supporting their potential as reversible therapeutic agents. To advance their clinical potential, we encapsulated the Survexins in human serum albumin-based nanoparticles (SurvexANs), leveraging the biocompatibility and high drug-loading capacity of albumin. SurvexANs were characterized and demonstrated stable morphology, controlled particle size and surface charge, and tunable drug-release properties. Importantly, encapsulation of Survexin5 preserved its inhibitory activity and kinetic properties while providing beneficial drug-release characteristics that may enable improved control of unintended cytotoxicity. These findings provide an important contribution to the exploration of nano-formulated inhibitors of CRM1-dependent nuclear export as a potential therapeutic approach for cancer therapy.

articles.title: From prognostic modeling to drug discovery: a metabolism-guided strategy for herbal small-molecule screening in gastric cancer.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion are tightly linked in gastric cancer (GC), yet metabolic signatures are rarely leveraged to guide treatment decisions or herbal small molecule drug discovery. METHODS: We profiled glycolysis, lipid, and tyrosine metabolism pathways across the TCGA-STAD and GSE62254 cohorts, identified prognostic metabolic subtypes, and distilled these findings into a three-gene risk signature (VCAN, NOS1, LCT). The signature was validated in the external GSE62254 cohort and assessed for associations with immune cell infiltration patterns, tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability status, and tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) scores. Rather than following the conventional compound-to-target screening paradigm, we reversed the pipeline: starting from the signature genes, we queried PubChem for herbal bioactive small molecules targeting the three signature proteins (VCAN, NOS1, and LCT) and evaluated candidates through molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and comprehensive ADMET profiling. The anti-GC activity of the leading candidate was further examined in AGS and HGC27 cells. RESULTS: Three prognostic metabolic subtypes with distinct survival outcomes and immune microenvironment compositions were identified.
