The model robustly stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups and showed significant correlations with immune cell infiltration patterns, tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability status, and TIDE scores. Notopterol (a furanocoumarin) and amentoflavone (a biflavonoid) emerged as the most promising hits. Notopterol, in particular, exhibited favorable drug-like properties and potent anti-GC activity: it suppressed the proliferation and migration of AGS and HGC27 cells in a concentration-dependent manner. DISCUSSION: These findings establish a metabolism-driven prognostic framework and nominate notopterol as a lead herbal-derived small molecule for further development in gastric cancer therapy; its correlations with immunotherapy-related features indicate potential utility for immunotherapy patient selection.

articles.title: Pretreatment with Commelina communis L. improves survival following influenza a virus infection and enhances innate interferon signaling.
articles.abstract: The objectives of this study were to evaluate the pre-exposure protective effects of Commelina communis L. (CCL) against influenza A virus (IAV) infection and to investigate its associated immunomodulatory mechanisms. Using RAW 264.7 cells and BALB/c mouse models, we demonstrated that CCL pretreatment reduced viral replication markers and suppressed viral protein expression in vitro. In vivo, prophylactic administration of CCL improved survival from 0% to 40% and attenuated body-weight loss following IAV challenge. Mechanistically, CCL enhanced the secretion of type I interferon IFN-β through activation of TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) and interferon regulatory factors 3 and 7 (IRF3/7). Activation of this signaling pathway was associated with STAT1/2 phosphorylation and increased expression of antiviral interferon-stimulated genes, including Isg20 and Isg56. Phytochemical profiling using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-UV-HRMS) identified four phytochemicals in CCL, among which rutin showed the greatest activity among the tested compounds in the in vitro screening assay. Collectively, these findings suggest that CCL and rutin may enhance host antiviral defense by modulating innate interferon signaling when administered before IAV exposure period.

articles.title: Effects of Chamaecostus cuspidatus leaf extract and p-coumaric acid on diabetes-associated vascular injury in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- induced wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Endothelial dysfunction plays a significant role in the cardiovascular consequences of diabetes. Persistent hyperglycemia and dyslipidaemia may increase oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. The present study aimed to evaluate the effects of Chamaecostus cuspidatus leaf extract and p-coumaric acid alone and in combination in a diabetic rat model induced by a high-fat diet and streptozotocin (40 mg/kg). The effects of the treatments were examined by biochemical parameters, oxidative stress parameters, antioxidant enzyme activities, histopathology and immunohistochemical assessment of vascular morphology and immunoreactivity of TXNIP, NLRP3 and caspase-1. The analytical findings tentatively supported the presence of p-coumaric acid in the methanolic leaf extract based on FTIR, GC- MS and HPLC investigations. HPLC examination indicated a similar retention time between the extract and the authentic p-coumaric acid standard, and the calculated concentration of p-coumaric acid equivalents was 15.30 μg/mL by single-point comparison. In diabetic rats, the combination treatment was associated with improved metabolic parameters compared with the diabetic disease control, including a 74% reduction in final blood glucose, together with reductions in total cholesterol, triglycerides and an improvement in HDL-C. Treatment enhanced antioxidant defence, with SOD, CAT, GSH and GPx increasing by 41%-100%, and decreased oxidative-stress indicators, such as ROS and MDA, by 38%-53%. Histopathological examination demonstrated comparatively preserved vascular architecture, accompanied by reduced TXNIP, NLRP3, and caspase-1 immunoreactivity. This finding suggests altered expression of inflammation-associated markers together with improvements in metabolic and oxidative state. In conclusion, combination therapy of C. cuspidatus leaf extract and p-coumaric acid exhibited positive effects on the vascular alterations associated with diabetes and may deserve further exploration as a combination method.

articles.title: Hyperbolic heterogeneous graph learning for adverse drug reaction prediction, candidate prioritization, and pathway-based interpretation in pharmacovigilance.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Adverse drug reaction (ADR) prediction remains challenging because spontaneous reporting data leave many exposure unit-ADR associations unobserved and provide limited support for candidate prioritization and mechanistic interpretation. METHODS: We developed MEG-HHGN, a mechanistic evidence-guided hyperbolic heterogeneous graph neural network. It represents exposure units as combinations of standardized drug names and routes of administration and integrates spontaneous reports with compounds, drug targets, ADR-related targets, and protein-protein interactions. Using 73,530 spontaneous reports collected in Jiangsu Province from 2010 to 2023, we evaluated MEG-HHGN against eight baseline methods through five-fold cross-validation. RESULTS: MEG-HHGN achieved AUC/AP/MCC values of 0.9550/0.9537/0.7917 in known-exposure-unit completion and 0.9090/0.9064/0.6587 in side-information-supported exposure-unit cold-start evaluation. Global scoring of unobserved exposure unit-ADR pairs produced a ranked candidate pool for pharmacovigilance review. Representative cases involving intravenous vinorelbine tartrate-myelosuppression and oral aspirin-proteinuria illustrated PPI-bridged and shared-target pathways, respectively. DISCUSSION: MEG-HHGN integrates route-aware prediction, candidate prioritization, and pathway-based interpretation in a unified framework to support signal triage, mechanistic hypothesis generation, and evidence review in post-marketing pharmacovigilance.

articles.title: A literature-informed pharmacokinetic framework for polymyxin B dosing during continuous renal replacement therapy: integrating renal function and extracorporeal clearance.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Existing population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) models for polymyxin B in patients receiving CRRT remain limited, and all of them have neglected the impact of membrane materials on drug adsorption. Recently, a few studies have attempted to construct integrated PK models by combining pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters derived from patients not receiving CRRT with CRRT-specific parameters. However, current integrated models only consider non-renal clearance and CRRT clearance (CLCRRT), excluding residual renal function (RRF). This study aimed to construct a literature-informed PK framework for polymyxin B incorporating intrinsic clearance (CLintrinsic, adjusted by CrCL to account for RRF) and CLCRRT, with CLCRRT comprising transmembrane (CLTM) and adsorptive (CLads) components. METHODS: CLCRRT allocation was set to 0% CLads for the PS membrane and 100% CLads for the AN69 membrane. The frameworks predictive performance was evaluated using two literature datasets (n = 53 and n = 30) and a prospective cohort (n = 10). Simulation analyses used PTA ≥90% as the criterion for adequate pharmacodynamic target attainment and a simulated probability of AUC0-24 h > 100 mg·h/L ≤ 14.5% as the exposure-exceedance threshold. RESULTS: The framework demonstrated accurate predictions of polymyxin B exposure in patients not receiving CRRT and those receiving CRRT (prediction error <30%). Filter type was the primary determinant of drug exposure, exceeding the effects of RRF or CRRT intensity. For the PS membrane (AV600S filter) and MIC = 0.5 mg/L pathogens, doses should be stratified based on CrCL with standard or lower doses. For the AN69 membrane (OXIRIS filter), a high-dose regimen (200 mg LD + 150 mg MD q12h) should be considered for infections with an MIC of 0.5 mg/L. An interactive Shiny application (https://xy3yx-cn.shinyapps.io/polymyxin-B-crrt-dosing/) was developed. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that filter type and RRF should be considered when individualizing polymyxin B dosing during CRRT. The proposed framework and the Shiny application are intended as research tools and require prospective clinical evaluation and therapeutic drug monitoring before routine clinical use.

articles.title: Roxadustat ameliorates bone microarchitectural deterioration in CKD-MBD rats in association with mitigated systemic micro-inflammation and restored FGF23-Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
articles.abstract: Elevated FGF23 is associated with bone microarchitectural deterioration in chronic kidney dis-ease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD). While roxadustat (a HIF-PHI) is established for the treatment of renal anemia, its potential bone-protective effects in CKD-MBD remain unclear. We investigated whether roxadustat ameliorates femoral microarchitectural deterioration in CKD-MBD rats in association with FGF23 downregulation and restoration of Wnt/β-catenin signaling. A CKD-MBD rat model was established by unilateral nephrectomy and adenine gavage, and animals were randomized into sham, model, and roxadustat (50 or 100 mg/kg, three times weekly) groups for 8 weeks. Renal function, hematological indices, calcium-phosphate parame-ters, and femoral microarchitecture were evaluated, and target protein levels (FGF23, FGFR1, DKK1, β-catenin) were assessed by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Roxadustat improved renal function, ameliorated the reduction in erythroid parameters, and restored calcium-phosphate homeostasis. Systemically, it mitigated micro-inflammation by reducing serum CRP and hepcidin, and downregulated serum FGF23 levels as well as tissue FGF23 expression in kidney and bone. In conclusion, the bone-protective effect of roxadustat occurs synchronously with systemic micro-inflammation mitigation, FGF23 downregulation, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling restoration. These findings highlight its pleiotropic therapeutic potential in CKD-MBD management, suggesting a synergistic benefit associated with both systemic metabolic recovery and local skeletal regulation.

articles.title: Lidocaine modulates interleukin-1β and interferon-α2 secretion in LPS with ATP stimulated human peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Local anesthetics are canonically used for analgesia and anti-arrhythmic therapy, but increasing evidence indicates additional anti-inflammatory properties, including modulation of purinergic signalling. A recent retrospective observational cohort study indicated that subcutaneous lidocaine-Hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) was associated with sustained improvements in quality of life in patients with neuropathic pain in post-COVID, but the underlying mechanism remains to be established. The aim of this study was to determine whether lidocaine and articaine, alone or in combination with HP-β-CD, modulate in vitro immune cell activation and cytokine secretion in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). METHODS: PBMCs were stimulated using phytohemagglutinin (PHA), lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or LPS combined with adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to engage P2X-associated inflammatory pathways, and compounds were applied both prior to and following stimulation. Cytokine secretion was quantified using a 13-plex immunoassay and cell activation was assessed by flow cytometry. RESULTS: Lidocaine-containing formulations attenuated cytokine secretion most prominently under conditions engaging ATP-dependent signaling, reducing interleukin-1β and interferon-α2, with interleukin-1β suppression being the most consistent effect across stimulation conditions. Articaine showed less consistent immunomodulatory effects than lidocaine, which may reflect its previously reported lack of purinergic receptor inhibition, while HP-β-CD alone did not influence immune activation or cytokine release under any condition. DISCUSSION: Together, these findings show that lidocaine-containing treatments can modulate cytokine responses in human PBMCs, particularly under LPS with ATP stimulation. These findings identify lidocaine as a modulator of ATP-dependent inflammatory signaling.

articles.title: Anlotinib suppresses homologous recombination via the E2F8-RAD51 axis to activate STING immunity and potentiate PARP inhibitor synthetic lethality in resistant small cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy that almost invariably acquires resistance to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, leading to early relapse. PARP inhibitors (PARPi) hold theoretical potential for SCLC due to universal TP53/RB1 deletion, but their monotherapy activity has limited efficacy in unselected relapsed patients. Anlotinib-a multi-target tyrosine kinase inhibitor-has recently been implicated in modulating DNA damage repair, raising the possibility of synergistic interaction with PARPi. However, the molecular basis of such synergy remains entirely unexplored. METHODS: Cisplatin-resistant SCLC cell models were established and characterized. A potent PARPi was screened, and the synergistic antitumor effects of talazoparib combined with anlotinib were evaluated via in vitro functional assays, multicellular tumor spheroid (MCT), and in vivo xenograft. Mechanisms were explored through transcriptomic, dual-luciferase reporter, rescue experiments, and immunohistochemical validation. RESULTS: The combination synergistically suppressed cell viability, anchorage-independent colony formation, and tumor growth versus monotherapies. Mechanistically, it significantly downregulated the E2F8 which was identified as a direct transcriptional activator of RAD51, as luciferase reporter assays showing that E2F8 overexpression increased wild-type RAD51 promoter activity. Rescue experiments demonstrated that E2F8 overexpression restored HR repair and reduced γ-H2AX levels in combination-treated cells. Furthermore, the combination activated the STING-TBK1-IRF3-IFNβ innate immune pathway and, in the MCT, significantly increased CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, CD45+HLA-DR+ activated immune cells and CD4+ helper T cells. CONCLUSION: Anlotinib potentiates the synthetic lethality of talazoparib in drug-resistant SCLC by suppressing E2F8-mediated RAD51 transcription, impairing homologous recombination repair, and inducing persistent DNA damage, while concurrently activating STING-dependent innate immunity. This dual mechanism provides a strong preclinical rationale for combining PARP inhibitors with anlotinib in relapsed SCLC, highlights E2F8/RAD51 as candidate biomarkers warranting further clinical validation, and supports future triplet regimens incorporating immune checkpoint inhibitors.

articles.title: Ginseng-Sanqi-Chuanxiong extract ameliorates hypertensive vascular aging through endothelial-smooth muscle cell crosstalk via the PPARγ/NF-κB axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular aging is an important pathological basis of hypertension and hypertension-associated target-organ injury. Ginseng-Sanqi-Chuanxiong (GSC) extract has been shown to have protective effects against vascular dysfunction; however, its mechanisms in hypertensive vascular aging remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: In this study, we investigated the protective effects and mechanisms of GSC in hypertensive vascular aging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical compounds present in GSC decoction were identified through ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight-mass spectrometry with elevated energy data acquisition (UPLC-Q-TOF/MSE) analysis. Network pharmacology was then used to predict the potential targets and signaling pathways. Ten-month-old spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) were treated with GSC for 4 months to evaluate vascular aging and target-organ injury. Lastly, endothelial-smooth muscle cell (EC-SMC) co-culture, molecular docking, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. RESULTS: UPLC-Q-TOF/MSE helped identify 55 compounds in GSC that were predominantly saponins, lactones, and phenolic-related constituents. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that PPARγ/NF-κB signaling could be a core regulatory pathway. GSC treatment reduced the systolic blood pressure while attenuating cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis, renal glomerular sclerosis and tubular injury, and hippocampal neuronal loss in the SHRs. GSC also alleviated vascular remodeling, vascular stiffness, and vascular senescence while decreasing inflammatory cytokine and senescence-related protein expression levels and regulating PPARγ/NF-κB signaling in vascular tissues. In the EC-SMC co-culture system, GSC intervention attenuated senescence in Ang-II-induced endothelial cells and inflammatory responses in co-cultured smooth muscle cells through endothelial-mediated paracrine regulation. The molecular docking and SPR assays further demonstrated direct interactions between PPARγ and GSC constituents, including kaempferol, senkyunolide H, and levistolide A. CONCLUSION: GSC attenuated hypertensive vascular aging through its protective effects associated with endothelial-mediated regulation of the PPARγ/NF-κB signaling pathway, providing scientific evidence of the vascular protective effects of GSC in hypertension.

articles.title: Epoxy fatty acids reduce corneal opacity and myofibroblast activation after alkali injury.
articles.abstract: Alkali-induced corneal injury causes epithelial damage, corneal opacity, stromal remodeling, and loss of transparency. Epoxy fatty acids (EpFAs), including epoxyeicosatrienoic acids (EETs) and epoxyeicosatetraenoic acids (EEQs), are rapidly hydrolyzed by soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH). However, their roles in the corneal response to chemical injury remain incompletely defined. We evaluated the effects of EET, EEQ, and the sEH-resistant EET analogs in human corneal fibroblasts, human corneal epithelial cells, and mouse models of NaOH- and ammonia-induced corneal injury. In human corneal fibroblasts, EET and EEQ attenuated TGFβ1-induced α-SMA and collagen III expression, while EEQ also reduced collagen 1A1 expression. In human corneal epithelial cells, EET and EEQ increased the MTT signal after NaOH exposure and increased the percentage of Ki67-positive cells in uninjured cultures. Chemical exposure increased cellular sEH activity in a cell type- and injury-dependent manner. In the mouse NaOH injury model, topical EET or EEQ reduced corneal opacity and stromal α-SMA and fibronectin staining. The sEH-resistant analogs M2 and M4 also reduced TGFβ1-induced α-SMA expression and corneal opacity. Combining EET with TPPU or EC5026 reduced corneal opacity earlier than EET alone. In the ammonia injury model, EET treatment and genetic deletion of sEH were associated with lower corneal opacity and neovascularization scores. Together, these findings show that pharmacological or genetic modulation of the sEH-EpFA pathway modifies the corneal response to alkali injury and is associated with reduced corneal opacity and myofibroblast-associated marker expression. Further studies are required to define the molecular mechanisms linking this pathway to TGFβ signaling and immune responses.

articles.title: Endpoint design in pulmonary arterial hypertension therapeutic trials permitting pediatric enrollment: a ClinicalTrials.gov registry analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric therapeutic development depends not only on age-appropriate dosing but also on endpoints whose administration and interpretation remain coherent across developmental stages. METHODS: An expanded ClinicalTrials.gov search was performed on 2 October 2026 using pulmonary hypertension terms plus the structured Child age filter (birth-17 years), while restricting eligibility to records first posted on or before 8 August 2026. The combined inventory contained 394 unique records. Seventy-two records formed the main analysis set; 69 were assigned to 57 traceable trial families and three continuation records remained unassigned at family level. Endpoint domains were counted once per family. RESULTS: Fifty-two families had registered outcomes available for domain analysis (42 first posted before 2017 and 10 in 2017-2026). Biomarker/laboratory measures occurred in 12/42 versus 9/10 families and functional capacity/activity in 38/42 versus 6/10. The study-level registered maximum permitted age was 18 years or younger in 14/42 earlier and 9/10 later families; this was used only for an age-scope sensitivity stratum and was not an eligibility criterion. In this age-scope stratum, several era contrasts attenuated, including PK/PD/dosing (9/14 vs. 7/9; difference +13.5 percentage points, 95% CI -24.4 to +43.6). A core-primary sensitivity analysis excluding four families whose registry records were updated after the eligibility cutoff produced the same qualitative pattern of no recent functional primary entries and wider uncertainty in the smaller later-era group. Five families with completely missing outcome modules were all in the earlier era; extreme-case analyses are reported in the supplement. CONCLUSION: Endpoint portfolios differed across registration eras, but age-scope composition, differential missingness, and incomplete historical registry reconstruction limit a temporal interpretation. Public endpoint descriptions should specify the clinical construct, measurement method, reporter or data source, capability rule, and handling of children unable to complete an assessment.

articles.title: Inhaled Glucocorticoids During Pregnancy: A Population-Level Drug Utilization Study in Denmark From 2001 to 2023.
articles.abstract: We investigated trends of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) use among pregnant women in Denmark from 2001 to 2023 using aggregated data from the Danish Health Data Authority, where recorded prescription redemptions in the National Prescription Register are linked to pregnancies recorded in the Danish Medical Birth Registry. Use of combination preparations (ICS and beta2-agonists) increased substantially (from 1.3 to 21 per 1000 pregnant women), corresponding to a 16-fold increase, while use of single-agent preparations (ICS) decreased gradually (from 17 to 11 per 1000 pregnant women). Combination preparations became more prevalent than single-agent preparations in 2020 among pregnant women, reflecting changes in treatment guidelines and recommendations in 2019. ICS use was higher before than during pregnancy in 2001 (22 vs. 18 per 1000 women) but lower before than during pregnancy in 2023 (30 vs. 32 per 1000 women), with the pattern reversing in 2015. Use during pregnancy was highest among the oldest women (≥ 40 years), with some variation over time, while it fluctuated substantially among the youngest women (≤ 19 years) and increased more steadily among women aged 20-39 years. Overall, our results highlight changes in ICS use among pregnant women that are well aligned with national and international asthma guidelines.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics and exposure-response analysis of acalabrutinib in patients with untreated mantle cell lymphoma in the ECHO trial.
articles.abstract: AIMS: The phase 3 ECHO trial demonstrated superior progression-free survival (PFS) with acalabrutinib plus bendamustine-rituximab (BR) versus placebo plus BR in treatment-naive (TN) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). This analysis characterizes the pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of acalabrutinib and ACP-5862 (active metabolite) when administered with BR and evaluates exposure-response (efficacy/safety) relationships based on ECHO data. METHODS: In ECHO, patients aged ≥65 years with TN MCL received BR plus acalabrutinib or placebo. Acalabrutinib (100 mg twice daily) or placebo was administered at study start until progressive disease or unacceptable toxicity. A pooled population PK analysis dataset included 975 patients for acalabrutinib and 580 patients for ACP-5862 from ECHO plus 10 clinical trials. Exposure-response analyses examined associations between exposure and PFS, best overall response (BOR), and adverse events (AEs) from ECHO. RESULTS: Population PK analysis showed that demographics (age, body weight, sex, ethnicity, race) and other intrinsic factors (mild or moderate renal impairment; mild or moderate hepatic impairment) had no meaningful effect on acalabrutinib/ACP-5862 exposure. No impact of co-administration with BR was observed on PK exposure. Exposure-efficacy analyses of ECHO data showed a flat relationship between acalabrutinib/ACP-5862 exposure and PFS and BOR. Exposure-safety analyses of ECHO data showed no clinically meaningful correlation between acalabrutinib/ACP-5862 exposure and selected safety outcomes (grade ≥3 AEs and events of clinical interest, AEs leading to dose modifications). CONCLUSION: This analysis supports a fixed 100 mg twice daily acalabrutinib dose, in combination with BR, as well-tolerated and efficacious in treatment of patients with TN MCL.

articles.title: Psychedelic experience intensity during ketamine treatment and antidepressant outcomes.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Ketamine is an effective antidepressant, but the role of acute subjective effects in treatment response remains unclear. Prior studies rely largely on dissociation measures focused on adverse events, which may not capture broader effects across multiple phenomenological domains. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether subjective psychedelic intensity during ketamine treatment, considered beyond an adverse-event framework, is associated with antidepressant outcomes. METHODS: In this retrospective longitudinal cohort study, 3,637 adults with moderate-to-severe depression received up to 4 doses of sublingual ketamine over 4 weeks within a telehealth-supported treatment program. Subjective effects were assessed using the Mindbloom Psychedelic Intensity (MPI) scale, a novel 5-item measure capturing emotional, cognitive, physical, visual, and auditory effects. Primary outcomes included end-of-treatment change in Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores, clinically significant change, and treatment response trajectories. Pre-registered analyses evaluated whether MPI scores at the midpoint of treatment were associated with antidepressant outcomes. RESULTS: Higher subjective intensity scores at 2 weeks were associated with greater reductions in depression severity at 4 weeks, increased likelihood of clinically significant change, and greater likelihood of membership in an improvement trajectory, independent of dose and other covariates. CONCLUSIONS: Subjective intensity of the ketamine experience was robustly associated with antidepressant outcomes. These findings suggest that subjective drug effects represent a clinically meaningful correlate of treatment response and highlight the importance of assessments designed to capture first-person experiences with ketamine, with implications for future mechanistic research and clinical care.

articles.title: Quality by design development of folic acid-engineered berberine nanoliposomes for targeted triple-negative breast cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains one of the most challenging breast cancer subtypes due to the lack of actionable molecular targets and the systemic toxicity associated with standard chemotherapy. Berberine chloride (BBR), a plant-derived isoquinoline alkaloid, exhibits promising anticancer activity; however, its poor solubility and limited bioavailability restrict therapeutic utility. Therefore, liposomal encapsulation was explored to improve BBR delivery, while folic acid functionalization was introduced to enhance preferential interaction with folate receptor-expressing TNBC cells. In this study, folic acid-decorated nanoliposomes were developed to enhance the targeted delivery of BBR to TNBC cells. BBR-loaded liposomes and folic acid-functionalized liposomes were prepared using the solvent injection method and optimized through a Quality-by-Design (QbD) framework. The optimized folate-modified formulation showed a mean particle size of 168.3 nm with an entrapment efficiency of 41.8%, while non-targeted liposomes exhibited a smaller size (95.6 nm) and slightly higher entrapment loading (47.5%). Both systems provided sustained drug release over 72 h, with folate-decorated liposomes demonstrating a more controlled release pattern. Cytotoxicity studies in MDA-MB-231 cells following 24 h of treatment revealed significantly enhanced antiproliferative activity of folate-functionalized nanoliposomes (IC50 = 24.72 μM) compared to non-targeted liposomes and free BBR. Increased intracellular reactive oxygen species generation following folate-mediated delivery suggested oxidative stress-associated cytotoxicity. Importantly, preliminary safety evaluation using Drosophila melanogaster confirmed the biocompatibility of the liposomal formulations. Overall, folic acid-decorated nanoliposomes substantially improve the therapeutic efficacy of berberine and offer a rational nanocarrier approach for TNBC management.

articles.title: Lipid-lowering, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects of Erythrina speciosa and its triterpenoids in acute dyslipidemia.
articles.abstract: Dyslipidemia is a health concern that contributes to metabolic and cardiovascular complications. The present study evaluated the anti-dyslipidemic potential of the chloroform fraction of Erythrina speciosa leaves and its isolated constituents, with particular emphasis on lipid regulation, redox balance, and inflammatory mediators. Chromatographic separation of the chloroform fraction led to the isolation of five triterpenoids, reported here for the first time from E. speciosa. The biological activity was assessed in a poloxamer-407-induced acute hyperlipidemia model in rats. Treatment with the chloroform fraction, isolated compounds, or atorvastatin significantly attenuated elevations in serum total cholesterol and triglycerides and improved low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C). These effects were accompanied by restoration of lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity, upregulation of hepatic LDL receptor (LDL-R), downregulation of fatty acid synthase (FAS), and suppression of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMG-CoA) reductase. Moreover, E. speciosa and its triterpenoids markedly alleviated oxidative stress and inflammation, as evidenced by reduced malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-κB) p65, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and interleukin (IL)- 1β and enhanced antioxidants. Molecular docking provided supportive computational evidence by predicting favorable binding interactions of the isolated compounds with NF-κB p65, LDL-R PCSK9 binding domain, and FAS. In conclusion, E. speciosa and its triterpenoids are promising candidates for the management of dyslipidemia and related inflammatory and oxidative disturbances.

articles.title: Machine learning pipeline for secretome biomarker discovery in colorectal cancer: from single-cell transcriptomics to functional validation.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) requires robust biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study aimed to identify secretome-associated genes with diagnostic, prognostic, and tumor-suppressive relevance in CRC, focusing on GUCA2B (uroguanylin). We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, pseudobulk differential expression, machine learning (ML), multi-omics, and in vitro functional assays (HCT-116 cells). ML consensus feature selection across four algorithms identified 20 shared features from 850 downregulated genes; eight genes, including GUCA2B, were selected by all four models, forming the finalized signature. GUCA2B was markedly reduced in CRC epithelium. A frozen eight-gene logistic model showed an apparent (training-set) AUC of 0.998 in TCGA-COADREAD and maintained discrimination in three independent cohorts (AUC = 0.881-0.974). Reduced GUCA2B expression correlated with adverse survival, promoter hypermethylation, and altered immune infiltration. In vitro, GUCA2B restoration induced intrinsic apoptosis (increased BAX, decreased BCL2), reduced viability, and impaired migration; because GC-C/cGMP dependence was not tested, these effects constitute receptor-mechanism-agnostic proof of concept. In conclusion, GUCA2B represents a candidate epithelial-restricted CRC biomarker and tumor-suppressive gene. While the frozen multi-gene model shows promise for diagnostic stratification and GUCA2B restoration demonstrates preliminary tumor-suppressive activity, the small discovery set (n = 23 pseudobulk samples), moderate feature-selection stability, and single-cell-line validation necessitate cautious interpretation. Prospective clinical validation and in vivo multi-model studies are required before diagnostic or therapeutic application.

articles.title: Antiplatelet Use in the Setting of Therapeutic Anticoagulation: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Patients receiving therapeutic oral anticoagulation (OAC) often have indications for antiplatelet therapy. Historically, antiplatelet agents have been used alongside therapeutic anticoagulation, increasing the risk of bleeding without a proven reduction in thrombosis. This scoping review summarizes recent evidence evaluating OAC monotherapy compared with combination therapy consisting of OAC plus antiplatelet agent among patients with atrial fibrillation and stable coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, and prosthetic heart valves. We searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, and International Pharmaceutical Abstracts to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating these strategies. Included studies enrolled adults receiving therapeutic anticoagulation across different cardiovascular disease states that reported efficacy and safety outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Published subgroup analyses of included RCTs were also reviewed. After screening 10,008 records, 11 RCTs met inclusion criteria. Evidence supporting OAC monotherapy was observed in patients with atrial fibrillation and stable coronary artery disease; OAC monotherapy consistently reduced bleeding without increasing ischemic events compared with combination therapy. Similar reductions in bleeding were observed in patients with cerebrovascular disease, although evidence remains limited by small sample size and early trial termination. Among patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with an indication for chronic anticoagulation, OAC monotherapy reduced bleeding without compromising ischemic outcomes. Evidence supporting discontinuation of antiplatelet therapy in patients with mechanical heart valves remains limited. Additional RCTs are needed to better define the role of antiplatelet therapy in cerebrovascular disease, prosthetic heart valves, and other high-risk populations.

articles.title: Initiation of lenacapavir with dose escalation in a patient receiving rifabutin: A case report with therapeutic drug monitoring.
articles.abstract: Lenacapavir is a first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor with long-acting pharmacokinetics that enable 6-monthly subcutaneous dosing after initiation with oral lead-in. Lenacapavir is a CYP3A4, UGT1A1 and P-gp substrate; inducers of these enzymes and P-gp can significantly decrease lenacapavir concentrations. In patients receiving lenacapavir for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), supplemental lenacapavir doses can be administered if rifabutin (moderate inducer) or rifampin (potent inducer) are initiated. However, these recommendations have not been extended to lenacapavir when used for HIV treatment, and little is known about initiating lenacapavir in patients on stable therapy with inducers. We describe a 30-year-old man with advanced HIV infection and disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex infection receiving rifabutin and concurrent darunavir/ritonavir in whom lenacapavir was initiated with a 50% increase in both oral (900 mg on Days 1 and 2) and subcutaneous loading doses (1390.5 mg on Day 1). Therapeutic drug monitoring using validated UPLC-MS/MS method demonstrated that lenacapavir plasma concentrations remained above the target of 15.5 ng/mL (4× protein-adjusted 95% effective concentration [PA-EC95]) over the dosing interval, with Cmax of 245.7 ng/mL and a projected Cmin of 19.5 ng/mL at 6 months. HIV viral load remained suppressed. This case demonstrates that dose-adjusted lenacapavir can achieve therapeutic exposures in the presence of pre-existing moderate induction. These findings provide clinically relevant pharmacological insight to support the use of lenacapavir in complex patients requiring rifamycin therapy.

articles.title: Case Report: Third-line QL1706, a bifunctional PD-1/CTLA-4 MabPair product, plus chemotherapy for primary small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the ureter.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the ureter is an extremely rare and aggressive malignancy with no established standard treatment strategy, particularly after progression on prior systemic therapy. CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old man with primary ureteral small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma underwent non-radical surgery followed by six cycles of etoposide, nedaplatin, and tislelizumab, without subsequent maintenance immunotherapy. The postoperative progression-free interval (PFS1) was approximately 39 months. Following recurrence, second-line etoposide and carboplatin were initiated, with tislelizumab reintroduced in the second cycle; the second-line progression-free survival (PFS2) was approximately 7 weeks. Third-line treatment consisted of QL1706, a bifunctional PD-1/CTLA-4 MabPair product comprising iparomlimab and tuvonralimab, combined with nab-paclitaxel and lobaplatin. QL1706 was administered for two cycles and discontinued because the patient declined further QL1706 treatment, whereas chemotherapy was administered for five cycles. Subsequent imaging showed tumor shrinkage, with the response assessed as stable disease. The third-line progression-free survival (PFS3), measured from treatment initiation to documented progression, was approximately 8 months. Treatment-related adverse events were tolerable. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that progression after prior PD-1-containing chemoimmunotherapy did not preclude subsequent disease control with a QL1706-containing chemotherapy regimen. The observed outcome supports further investigation of this combination as a potential salvage strategy for recurrent or refractory ureteral small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma. However, the individual contribution of QL1706 cannot be distinguished from that of concomitant chemotherapy in this single case.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Dosing Evaluation for Sedation in Neonates Undergoing Therapeutic Hypothermia.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Recently, dexmedetomidine has replaced opioids for sedation in neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) patients with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). The study objectives were to describe dosing patterns, evaluate compliance, and compare effectiveness and safety between the original (pre-implementation) and revised (post-implementation) in-house dexmedetomidine dosing guidelines. STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study that included neonates with HIE admitted to a level IV NICU for therapeutic hypothermia comparing two dexmedetomidine dosing regimens: (1) pre-implementation: starting dose of 0.05 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.05 μg/kg/h every 6 h as needed, and (2) post-implementation: 0.2 μg/kg/h followed by titration by 0.1 μg/kg/h every 30-60 min as needed. RESULTS: A total of 106 neonates were included: 50 in the pre-implementation group and 56 in the post-implementation group. Compliance to post-implementation formulary recommendations was 69.6% for initial doses, 62.5% for dose increases, and 44.6% for dose decreases. An increased odds of opioid exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 7.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.59-51.5, p = 0.02) and greater proportion of bradycardia (21.4% vs. 4%, p = 0.03) were observed in the post-implementation group. No significant differences in effectiveness end points or hypotension were observed between groups (p ≥ 0.05). CONCLUSION: Compliance with formulary-recommended dexmedetomidine dosing was variable and dose decreases were common in the post-implementation group. The post-implementation dosing approach was not associated with improved effectiveness outcomes (sedation) but was associated with greater opioid exposure and more bradycardia, supporting the need for further prospective evaluation to determine the optimal dexmedetomidine dosing in neonates undergoing HIE.

Metabolite Identification of Sauchinone in Rats using HPLC-HRMS and Its Metabolism in Rat, Mouse and Human Liver Microsomes.
articles.abstract: Sauchinone is a diastereomeric lignan extracted from Saururus chinensis with various physiological effects. To date, the metabolism of sauchinone remains limited. This study investigated the in vivo metabolism of sauchinone in rats, as well as its in vitro metabolic stability and interspecies differences in metabolism.High-performance liquid chromatography and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HPLC-HRMS) was used to detect and characterize sauchinone metabolites in male rats following oral administration at 50 mg/kg. Under the current conditions, 5 metabolites were exclusively detected in faeces, whereas only the unchanged parent compound was observed in plasma and urine. The major metabolic pathways were demethylenation and reduction.In the metabolic stability study, sauchinone was rapidly metabolized in rat liver microsomes (T1/2 = 11.49 min), whereas it showed moderate (T1/2 = 49.96 min) and slow (T1/2 = 88.26 min) metabolic stability in human and mouse liver microsomes, respectively. Metabolic profiles of sauchinone were similar across rat, mouse and human liver microsomes, with a total of 4 metabolites identified.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics and Initial Bolus Dosing of Furosemide in Children on ECMO.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is an established technology that provides life-saving mechanical support for critically ill children. In these children, fluid overload is commonly treated with furosemide; however, optimal dosing of furosemide is unknown in children supported with ECMO because ECMO may alter furosemide exposure. In this work, human blood-primed ex vivo experiments quantified red blood cell partitioning and extraction of furosemide by the ECMO circuit. Furosemide partitioned into red blood cells but was not extracted by ECMO circuits. These data then parameterized a pediatric physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of furosemide in children with and without ECMO. Next, plasma furosemide concentrations from 10 critically ill children supported by ECMO were used to evaluate PBPK model performance, with the optimized model achieving average fold error and absolute average fold error of 1.02 and 1.67, respectively. The optimized PBPK model also predicted that ECMO increases apparent volume of distribution by a median of > 30% in neonates and infants. Finally, population PBPK simulations with the optimized PBPK model provided initial bolus doses that most rapidly achieve steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations with and without ECMO. These calibrated initial bolus doses achieved steady-state plasma furosemide concentrations > 3 h faster than continuous infusions without an initial bolus dose, and this improvement was most pronounced in neonates and infants on ECMO. Overall, this work supports comparatively larger initial bolus doses for neonates and infants on ECMO, and provides calibrated initial bolus doses based on plasma exposure for critically ill children.

articles.title: Adjunct Low-Dose Dexmedetomidine for Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Children: An Exploratory Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective sedation in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) is complicated by the adverse effects of benzodiazepines and opioids. Dexmedetomidine may provide a benzodiazepine-sparing alternative with distinct pharmacologic properties. OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that adjunct, fixed low-dose, no-bolus dexmedetomidine would reduce midazolam and fentanyl exposure per ventilator-day in mechanically ventilated children. METHODS: In a triple-blind randomized controlled trial, 60 mechanically ventilated patients aged 1 month to 12 years were randomized to standard sedation (continuous midazolam and fentanyl) plus low-dose dexmedetomidine (a fixed-rate continuous infusion at 0.2 µg/kg/h without a loading bolus) or matched placebo (0.9% normal saline). In both groups, midazolam and fentanyl were titrated per protocol to achieve the target Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) level. RESULTS: Among 60 randomized children, adjunct fixed low-dose dexmedetomidine did not reduce the prespecified primary outcome of fentanyl or midazolam exposure per ventilator-day. Median fentanyl exposure per ventilator-day was 70.0 µg·kg-1·day-1 in the control group and 90.6 µg·kg-1·day-1 in the dexmedetomidine group; median midazolam exposure per ventilator-day was 7.0 mg·kg-1·day-1 and 9.1 mg·kg-1·day-1, respectively. Neither primary comparison remained statistically significant after Holm correction. In an unadjusted secondary analysis, the median time to first successful extubation was 6 days in the dexmedetomidine group and 15 days in the control group. This finding was exploratory and was not confirmed by the prespecified competing-risk or longitudinal ventilation analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Adjunct fixed low-dose dexmedetomidine without a loading bolus did not reduce fentanyl or midazolam exposure per ventilator-day. Early sedative-analgesic exposure was higher with dexmedetomidine, and the apparent early-extubation signal was exploratory and was not confirmed by competing-risk or longitudinal analyses of ventilation.

articles.title: Tanshinone IIA Alleviates Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Acute Kidney Injury in Mice by Activating SIRT1/PINK1-Mediated Mitophagy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a critical clinical condition closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction. Tanshinone IIA has been shown to exert protective effects against AKI; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate whether Tanshinone IIA mitigates lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced AKI through SIRT1/PINK1-mediated mitophagy. METHODS: A mouse model of AKI was established by intraperitoneal injection of LPS. Renal function was assessed by measuring serum creatinine (Scr) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels. Renal histopathological changes were evaluated using hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining. Mitochondrial function was assessed by measuring adenosine triphosphate (ATP) content, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), and mitochondrial membrane potential in renal tissue. The expression of mitophagy-related markers was analyzed by Western blotting. RESULTS: Lipopolysaccharide treatment significantly increased Scr and BUN levels and induced marked renal pathological injury in mice compared with those in the control group. Tanshinone IIA intervention reduced Scr and BUN levels and alleviated renal tissue damage. Mitochondrial function analysis showed that Tanshinone IIA restored the LPS-induced reduction in ATP content, suppressed excessive mitochondrial ROS generation, and stabilized the mitochondrial membrane potential. Mechanistic analyses further demonstrated that Tanshinone IIA upregulated the LPS-induced expression of SIRT1 and PINK1, increased the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, and promoted p62 degradation. CONCLUSIONS: Tanshinone IIA protects against LPS-induced AKI by improving mitochondrial function through the activation of SIRT1/PINK1-mediated mitophagy.

Selexipag as a Therapeutic Alternative for Treprostinil-Induced Thrombocytopenia in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Parenteral prostacyclin pathway agent-induced thrombocytopenia may require dose reduction or therapy discontinuation to mitigate the adverse events. However, the pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) guidelines do not suggest any strategy to overcome treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia. Selexipag is an oral, non-prostanoid, selective IP receptor agonist. This is the first case report proposing the use of selexipag, due to its minimal thrombocytopenia risk, when severe treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia occurs in practice. A 66-year-old woman presented to the hospital with new-onset PAH and right ventricular dysfunction. Due to the high mortality risk, the patient was initially started on intravenous treprostinil. The clinical course was complicated by probable treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia. Due to the need for prostacyclin pathway therapy, the decision was made to switch from intravenous treprostinil to oral selexipag. The nadir platelet count was 30,000/μL. Approximately 72 h after discontinuation of treprostinil and maintaining selexipag 1600 mcg twice daily, the platelet count improved to 46,000/μL on the day of discharge. Several days after discharge, the platelet count further improved to 55,000/μL. The repeated platelet count 1 month after discharge normalized to 329,000/μL. Our case report described the successful use of selexipag to overcome treprostinil-induced thrombocytopenia, owing to its limited effect on platelet aggregation.
